In the release workflows I inspected, such as `.github/workflows/ci.yml:20-24`, the only gate is `npm run release:check`, which now delegates to this `check`. This new `check` compiles and rebuilds generated artifacts but no longer ends with the previous `git diff --exit-code -- ...`, so a PR can change source data, let the runner mutate generated files, and still exit 0 with stale checked-in artifacts. Please keep a final drift check after the compile/build steps.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make public estate hrefs resolve from the public manifest**

When this manifest is written to `reports/core-thesis/unmapped-sections/data.json`, `public_href` resolves relative to that file as `reports/core-thesis/unmapped-sections/unmapped-sections/estates/...`, but the public estate ledgers are written under `reports/core-thesis/unmapped-sections/estates/...`. Any consumer that follows the manifest hrefs will get 404s; the public manifest needs `estates/${packet.estate_id}.json` here or a clearly root-relative path.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Materialize required inputs before the permanent build**

In this committed tree the generated inputs read by the build script, including `data/intake/security-state-organism-source-routes.json`, `data/project/security-state-estate-alignment.json`, and `data/project/security-state-work-packages.json`, are not present; they are only produced by the temporary materializer. Because this permanent workflow invokes the build script directly on workflow_dispatch/push/PR, a clean checkout exits immediately with `ENOENT` before any validation can run, so the workflow cannot validate the repository until those inputs are committed or generated in this job.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use the entity organ key expected by the generator**

All entity rows use `candidate_organs`, but both the materializer and validator read `candidate_organ_ids`. With this registry, materialization silently builds every `ENT-*` package with empty `organ_ids`, and validation then throws `TypeError: x.candidate_organ_ids is not iterable` on the first entity after the generated files exist. Rename/populate the key the scripts actually consume, or update the scripts to read this schema.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recompute the registry facet counts**

The source rows contain only 7 distinct `jurisdiction` values and 38 distinct entries across their `subjects` arrays, so the committed counts of 8 and 39 overstate both facets. Any report or downstream consumer using this metadata will publish inaccurate coverage, and the new validator does not catch it because it validates only `sources.sources.length`; derive and validate these values from the source rows.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Render the entire frozen source denominator**

When a frozen source has no timeline event—as happens with `M05-S02-L2-SRC-009`, the Companies House entity record—deriving `usedSources` exclusively from timeline IDs drops it from `source_records` and the HTML table. The resulting report claims nine source records while `sources_used` and the table headed “Frozen source denominator” contain only eight, preventing readers from auditing all evidence included in that denominator; render the full source registry or ensure every denominator source is otherwise included.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include sources used outside the decision chain**

When the report is built, `usedIds` is derived only from `public_decision_chain`, so `M05-S02-L3-SRC-007` is omitted from `source_records` and the HTML source denominator even though the other-vendors responsibility entry and proposition P06 use its competitive-onboarding evidence. The page consequently reports 10 official sources but renders only nine and leaves those claims without their supporting source; collect references from every matrix section or include the full source array.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve source URLs in the generated HTML**

When readers use the committed HTML report, the source table renders only the escaped title and class and drops `row.url`, so none of the six evidence records can be opened or verified from the public report surface. Render the title as an escaped link, as the preceding sprint report builders do, rather than requiring readers to locate the separate JSON artifact.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Coordinate host throttling across matrix runners**

Each offset is measured from the time its independent matrix runner reaches the refresher, not from a shared workflow start time. With `max-parallel: 12`, runner provisioning, checkout, setup, build, and validation can vary by more than six seconds, so absolute GDELT request times can still overlap or arrive out of order despite these offsets, reproducing the 429 burst this change is intended to prevent. Anchor delays to a shared timestamp or serialize the host's requests across jobs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude the response Date from metadata fingerprints**

For any route that succeeds only through the new HEAD fallback, the HTTP `Date` header normally changes on every request. Including it in the fingerprint therefore makes identical resources appear changed on every orbit; the comparison below then emits a `changed_metadata_fingerprint` candidate even when the URL, validators, and content metadata are unchanged, polluting the change and candidate ledgers.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Normalize legacy state before detecting changes**

When this version reads an existing `m04g-global-circulation-orbit@1` state file, prior observations contain `sha256` and no `fingerprint_sha256` or `success_mode`. These comparisons consequently mark every previously successful route as changed on the first upgraded run even when its body and headers are identical, emitting false changed-source candidates. Use the same `prior.sha256` and default-content fallbacks already applied when recording the prior value.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce the non-promotion boundary strings**

Do not skip `promotes_to` and `graph_effect`: changing them to values such as `confirmed` or `promote` still passes this validator because the remaining loop only rejects truthy booleans. The workflow rebuilds the report from the altered plan before validating it, so its deterministic-product check also accepts the new values, allowing the plan and published report to contradict the sprint’s candidate-only, graph-inert boundary.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the fixed M-04G denominator requirement**

Include `same_m04g_denominator_required` in the required-controls check. If that field is removed or changed to `false`, validation and the regression test still succeed, while the builder faithfully publishes the weakened contract; this defeats the sprint’s explicit requirement to rerun the same 96-route denominator.

The holder list is not referentially valid against `constitutional_roles`: R5 and R7 use the undeclared `public authority`, while R6 stores `represented_person where individual refusal is legally or ethically indispensable` rather than the declared `represented_person` role. Any domain test or consumer resolving holders by role name therefore cannot identify these holders, despite `all_r_levels_have_named_holders_and_mechanisms` being set to true; represent conditions separately and add or reference a defined public-authority role.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the leg open until an affected-person chain is tested**

When this frozen artifact is used to close S03-L2, it violates the lane's terminal contract in `data/project/m05-answerable-power-sprint-03-plan.json:124`, which requires adjudication against one exact administrative system and one affected-person chain. This dataset instead aggregates two systems and lists participant action packets and person-level source-to-debt chronologies as future acquisitions, so it never tests the APC mechanisms together on a single source→action→contest→outcome chain. Leave the leg open or add the required chain before marking the domain test frozen.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the four frozen system IDs**

If a system is accidentally duplicated or replaced while the array remains four entries long, this validator and the new test both pass, and the builder publishes the altered denominator as four valid systems. Because the dataset is marked `bounded_domain_test_frozen`, validate the expected `system_id` set (and uniqueness), not only its length, so CI detects drift from the four named cases.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Downgrade the incomplete case from R5**

For the Homes for Ukraine evidence shipped here, this R5 claim contradicts the file's own `minimum_r5_test`: residual-custody/deletion reconciliation is required at lines 85–94, while this proposition acknowledges that complete residual deletion is absent at lines 384–387 and the acquisition list still requests the missing security/accreditation and custody records. Because the builder and validator then publish and enforce this as the domain's R5 positive control, the report overstates the observed result; keep it candidate/partial until every declared minimum is supported, or explicitly revise the minimum.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Classify routine HTTP failures before enforcing the health gate**

When a route's final candidate returns an ordinary client error such as 400, 404, or 405—or a redirect without a `Location` header—`classifyFailure` reaches this fallback and records `unclassified`. Since `coverage_healthy` requires `unclassified_failures === 0` and the workflow exits nonzero otherwise, one stale or malformed external endpoint can fail every scheduled orbit even though its failure is fully understood; add explicit client/redirect classifications and consume the `redirect_unresolved` result flag.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Write the checksum of the receipt file named in the manifest**

The `.sha256` manifest names `m04g-source-ecology-v2-receipt.json`, but its digest is computed from compact `JSON.stringify(receiptCore)`, while the named file contains the larger `receipt` object, pretty-printing, and a trailing newline. Consequently `sha256sum -c m04g-source-ecology-v2-proof.sha256` always fails, making the uploaded proof artifact unverifiable; hash the exact serialized bytes written to the receipt or label this as a logical core digest rather than a file checksum.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply no-adverse checks before promoting beyond A2**

Restricting this check to requests for exactly A3 or A4 lets A5 and A6 manifests bypass the inherited no-adverse requirement. Because `reached.A3` also omits `modeNoAdverse`, a manifest with every adverse, recommendation, influence, and consultation flag set to `true` can request A6 and receive `conformant: true` with a computed maximum of A6.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cap levels when critical blockers remain open**

Only validating that `open_blockers` is an array leaves its contents completely disconnected from level computation. For example, an A1 manifest can retain `open_blockers: ['no independent reproduction']`, assert `observations.independent_reproduction: true`, and still be accepted, even though the reconciliation specification says open critical blockers cap the claim below the affected level and documented contradictions are machine-detectable.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve URLs for the excluded search results**

When anyone audits or reproduces this 15-result capture, none of the eight excluded rows identifies the underlying result URL, unlike Wave 01's excluded records. Generic reasons such as “machine-translated duplicate” cannot prove that eight distinct results were observed or that the exclusions and deduplication were applied correctly, so `raw_results_observed: 15` and the resulting denominator are not auditable; retain the source URL for every excluded result.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recompute declared counts from audited rows**

When a row's role or disposition changes without manually updating `audit.counts`, this loop only compares the stored counters with fixed literals rather than deriving them from the rows. For example, changing R001 away from `counterpower_control_retained` makes the builder emit `report.counts.counterpower_controls: 0` while the audit still declares 1, yet validation passes because the report checks omit that control count. Recompute the counts from `audit.rows` and compare both the audit and report against those derived values.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make the validator import side-effect free**

When this validator is run against a checkout whose generated manifest or report has drifted, importing the builder evaluates its top-level writes before lines 46–47 read those artifacts. I verified that changing the report's publication status to `published` and then invoking the validator caused the import to restore the committed report and validation to return `OK`. Move manifest computation into a side-effect-free module or guard the builder's write path so validation remains non-destructive and can detect existing drift.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prevent validation from rebuilding the artifacts it checks**

When the validator is run against a stale or corrupted manifest/report, importing this module executes the builder's top-level code, including the writes at `build-k0-wave03-field-adjudication.mjs:115-129`, before `validateWave03Field` reads those artifacts. Consequently, even changing the committed report schema to an invalid value is silently repaired and the standalone validator exits successfully, so it cannot detect drift in the generated products it claims to validate. Move generation behind a direct-execution guard or put the manifest computation in a side-effect-free module.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Derive Wave 03 completion from its audit**

When the Wave 03 field-adjudication artifact and aggregate denominator drift apart, this check still passes because it only verifies the status string that it is meant to substantiate; `validateK0()` never reads `data/research/k0-wave03-field-adjudication.json`, and that artifact is also absent from the aggregate release scope. Validate the audit's identity/completion state—or its release manifest—before accepting `discovery_complete_field_adjudication_complete`, otherwise the aggregate report can claim completed adjudication without being bound to the underlying review.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Consequently, a stale or corrupted generated artifact is silently repaired and validation reports success rather than detecting the drift; for example, changing a report row and running the validator restores the row and prints `OK`. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include the embedded Wave 05 audit in the release hash**

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Align review states with denominator dispositions**

Once denominator execution assigns a documented disposition such as `retained_candidate_only`, `identity_ambiguous`, `source_unavailable`, or `positive_binding_correction_control`, the field-record schema rejects the row because this enum instead permits differently named states such as `selection_unresolved`, `requires_named_acquisition`, and `positive_control`. The denominator's `records` ledger therefore cannot represent several of its own declared outcomes without an undefined translation; use the protocol's disposition vocabulary consistently or specify and validate that mapping.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Render the actual execution-record count**

When denominator execution adds any records, `data.json` correctly derives `execution_records` from `denominator.records.length`, but the generated public HTML will continue to display zero because this card is hard-coded. That makes the report contradict its own generated data during the next planned execution wave; interpolate `report.counts.execution_records` here instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the frozen record against its manifest entry**

When SG-01 is superseded, this only confirms that the manifest JSON still contains the known digest string; it neither recomputes the digest from `manifest.entries` nor compares the frozen record's bytes with its stored hash. For example, changing `record.stable_propositions[0].text` or deleting every manifest entry while retaining `combined_sha256` makes both the validator and adversarial test pass, so the immutable checkpoint can be corrupted undetected.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make manual dispatch use a populated ref**

For the declared `workflow_dispatch` trigger, `github.head_ref` is empty because that context is populated for pull-request events, so this job is always skipped when manually dispatched. Moreover, the later `EXPECTED_HEAD` value also comes from `github.event.pull_request`. As a result, the advertised manual recovery path can never materialize the patches; use `github.ref`/`github.sha` for dispatches or remove that trigger.

On every `npm run build:pages`, the builder first copies the entire `reports` directory, while this denylist removes only the dedicated `reports/core-thesis/status-sovereignty` subtree. body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep blind-review identity keys out of Pages**

When the Pages artifact is built, `tools/build-pages.mjs` recursively copies `data` and `reports`, and its updated exclusion list does not remove any Wave 16–18 counter-selector products; running `npm run release:check` leaves this registry at `dist/data/project/counter-selector-external-review-export-registry.json`. Consequently, this identity mapping is deployed despite the registry declaring `staged_nonpublic_source_custody` and `released_to_reviewer: false`, so anyone given an export token can directly deanonymize all six review packets and compromise the planned external review. Exclude the staged counter-selector contracts, registries, reports, and especially this identity-key registry from Pages, and validate their absence.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Assign the report schema after spreading the intake record**

Every build overwrites the intended `status-sovereignty-institutional-gate-first-pass-report@1` value because `record` already contains its intake `schema_version`. Consequently, both generated report JSON files identify themselves as intake records even though their added `first_pass_id`, `counts`, and `release_manifest` fields violate that intake schema's `additionalProperties: false`, so schema-dispatching or validating consumers will reject or misclassify them.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the record against the declared JSON schema**

When a schema-required field that is not separately hard-coded here—such as `as_of` or `title`—is removed and the products and manifest are rebuilt, the focused workflow still passes because these checks only inspect three constants inside the schema and never validate `r` against it. This allows structurally invalid intake records to pass the new validation gate despite the schema declaring them invalid.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude every publication-blocked artifact from Pages**

In the Pages build, `tools/build-pages.mjs` copies both `data` and `docs`, but its publication hold list does not remove the new release manifest or milestone. Consequently, this step succeeds while `dist/data/project/status-sovereignty-natsec100-denominator-first-pass-release-manifest.json` and `dist/docs/milestones/ssc-natsec100-denominator-first-pass.md` are published, contradicting the SSC-H01 publication boundary; add them to the exclusion/validation lists and assert their absence here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the intake against the committed schema**

These checks validate three properties of the schema document itself, not whether the intake conforms to it. A committed intake that removes required fields such as `title`, adds an unexpected top-level property, uses an invalid `as_of`, or replaces `boundaries` with `{}` still passes the focused validator and adversarial suite, despite violating this commit's strict schema and potentially producing malformed custody products.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the report schema identifier after spreading the record**

Because `...record` follows the report-specific `schema_version`, the input record overwrites it. Both generated `data.json` products therefore identify themselves as `status-sovereignty-open-obligation-first-pass@1` rather than the declared `status-sovereignty-natsec100-denominator-first-pass-report@1`, so consumers dispatching or validating by schema cannot distinguish the report from its intake record.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

When a producer adds an unknown or misspelled property, this path only runs the hand-written assertions and never evaluates `counter-selector-exception-falsification.schema.json`. For example, adding `sources[0].typo` still passes `validateCounterSelectorWave20()` and is propagated into the generated audit registry even though the source schema declares `additionalProperties: false`, so the workflow can accept and publish data that violates its declared contract.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove named platforms from the blind-review input**

The B02 `support_context` passed to reviewers names KPMG, Azure, Cloudflare, GitHub, and Stripe, even though this file's input contract prohibits sponsor/platform names and the method says those cues are removed; B01 similarly exposes the TH3 and dbsqlfuzz product names. For reviewers receiving these packets, the named infrastructure makes the underlying artifact substantially easier to identify, so the four completed passes do not satisfy the stated blind-review procedure. Strip or generalize these names and add the prohibited-cue scan used by Wave 27.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin lineage hashes to the referenced releases**

These assertions accept any syntactically valid digest rather than verifying the actual Wave 26 and Wave 27 manifest hashes. A source file with either value replaced by an arbitrary 64-hex string passes `validateSource`, and rebuilding all derived products then passes the exact-file checks, leaving a release that claims nonexistent parent or sibling provenance. Compare both fields with the corresponding committed manifests or their expected constants.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recompute world signatures before accepting the build**

When a serialized build's top-level world data is corrupted, validation can still pass because this code only checks that the stored signatures look like hashes and that the separately serialized custody chain remains internally valid. For example, changing a world's `allocation.amount_paid_to_affected` after compilation while leaving its chain and signature untouched produces no validation errors, allowing an inconsistent artifact to be accepted and consumed by the v16 compiler. Recompute each signature from the current world state and verify that the top-level fields match the corresponding custody payloads.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Derive integrity flags from the compiled controls**

When a serialized v16 artifact has a control modified after compilation, the validator trusts the stored integrity booleans rather than re-evaluating them. For example, changing `compiled.controls[0].graph_effect` to `asserted` still yields no validation errors because `control_integrity.all_graph_effect_none` remains `true`; similarly, arbitrary changes to a base control's failure class are accepted. Recompute these predicates and derived collections from `compiled.controls` so the validator cannot qualify a corrupted floor.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require claim appeals before classifying a world complete**

When `claims.appeal_available` is `false` but the governance-level appeal route is present, the compiler still marks the world as a complete collective distribution. Changing only that field in the positive fixture passes validation and preserves `complete_collective_distribution: true`, despite claim appeal being explicitly modeled as part of the custody state. Include claim-level appeal availability in this completion predicate so an unappealable claim decision cannot qualify as complete.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recompute world invariants when validating build artifacts**

When a serialized build is validated, the top-level world fields and custody-chain payloads are independent objects, but this loop trusts the stored `full_population_paid`, `full_net_exhaustion`, metrics, flags, and signature strings. For example, changing a subgroup's `actual_amount` to `999999` in the generated JSON while leaving those cached values and the chain untouched still returns no validation errors. This lets a corrupted allocation artifact pass, so the validator should recompute the allocation invariants and signatures and compare the top-level world to the sealed payload.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate promotion requirements by identity**

The manifest is described as adding a specific frozen set of allocation-formula evidence requirements, but this check only counts unique strings. Replacing any required entry—for example the affected-population requirement—with `placeholder` still passes source validation, compilation, and build validation while silently removing that category from the real-case promotion boundary. Validate membership against the required set (or at least enforce the defined requirement namespace and categories), rather than accepting any forty strings.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Remove payload chunks during dispatched cleanup**

When `workflow_dispatch` targets the trusted materializer ref, the checkout already contains the four `data/transport/ssc-rd04-a05-payload-*.b64` files that this workflow reads from that ref. These cleanup commands remove only the rearm receipt and workflow, so the resulting commit retains all four transport chunks despite being labeled transport-free. Delete the payload chunks too, or prevent dispatch from refs that contain them.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject all positive resumability and handoff states**

These checks reject only the exact string `supported`, while the schema leaves both fields unconstrained. A later audit can therefore use another positive representation such as `supported_with_receipt`, `established`, or even `true`; validation, product generation, and the workflow will all pass while the published counts and boundaries still claim zero resumable projects and handoffs. Validate the exact allowed state for each lane or use a closed enum that excludes every positive state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind world state to the validated custody chain**

When the emitted JSON is read back by the validation command, each top-level world object and its custody-chain payload are independent copies. Modifying a field such as `world.release.binding_scope` therefore leaves the chain hashes untouched, and this validator accepts the corrupted artifact because it neither recomputes the world signature nor compares the top-level state with the sealed payload. It also accepts a world whose chain and head are both omitted, since an empty chain produces no errors and both sides of the head comparison are `undefined`; require a nonempty chain and verify that its sealed payloads and signatures match the current world state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify composed controls against their snapshots**

For a serialized v18 build, altering an inherited control—for example, changing `controls[0].failure_class`—still yields a successful validation as long as its ID and the precomputed integrity booleans remain unchanged. The snapshot fields are checked only for hash-shaped text, while neither those hashes nor the custody-chain snapshots are bound back to the current `controls`, so the validator can qualify a corrupted twenty-control floor. Recompute the applicable snapshots from the validated content, or validate against the source/base build used to produce them.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate aggregate values against the retained report**

When retained report tables or `sourceLedger.normalized_facts` are changed while the expected totals remain unchanged, `buildA05()` copies the ledger values into the published quarterly fields and refreshes the release manifest, but this validation only checks that three headings exist in `reportText`. It never reparses the retained tables or compares the ledger facts with them, so incorrect quarterly values—and even a report contradicting the pinned totals—can pass the workflow and be published as validated evidence.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the source against its declared schema**

When a source edit violates fields constrained only by the new schema, the validation workflow still succeeds because `validateSource` never loads or applies that schema. For example, changing `program_id` or a source-record URL to arbitrary strings passes the focused validator and, after rebuilding the committed products, the exact-product checks as well; malformed identifiers and records can therefore be published. Apply the declared schema or add equivalent comprehensive checks before deriving the outputs.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin every published empirical count**

Counts such as `named_outgoing_entities`, `named_incoming_entities`, `complete_outgoing_state_packages`, `bounded_collaborations_authorized`, and `adversarial_mutations` are part of the stated permanent empirical result but are omitted from these assertions; for example, setting `named_incoming_entities` to 999 succeeds. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require the nine named handoff components**

When one of the contract's component keys is deleted and replaced by an unrelated key, this length-only check still passes; for example, replacing `outgoing_intent_or_departure` with `foo` is accepted and propagated to the public artifacts. The accompanying schema also allows arbitrary component properties, so schema validation alone would not protect consumers expecting the nine dimensions listed by `component_order`. When a world's actual notice record has fewer than 100 deliveries but its frozen public claim still reports 100, this expression marks `full_notice_delivery` as true. Because fixture validation permits that discrepancy, even a world with zero sent and delivered notices compiles with `full_notice_delivery_worlds: 8`, passes build validation, and can retain a complete informed-choice classification. Derive this metric from `world.notice.delivered_count` rather than the public claim being tested.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind current lineage to the baseline reference versions**

When both the approved and executed lineage values are changed to the same unrelated version, this equality check still marks the lineage current because the expected version in each tuple is discarded. For example, setting both subgroup-frame values to `EVIL-V2` while the baseline references `HTE-SUBGROUP-FRAME-V1` passes fixture validation and leaves one world classified as complete assurance. Compare each lineage value with the corresponding baseline reference so version succession cannot be treated as current merely because approved and executed agree.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revalidate the inherited controls before asserting integrity**

When a serialized v35 artifact has any of its first 36 controls altered, the standalone validator still returns success because it checks only the array length, the final PC-37 control, and precomputed `control_integrity` booleans. I verified that changing `controls[0].control_id` and setting its `graph_effect` to `asserted` produces no validation errors, so the advertised preserved v34 floor can be corrupted without detection. Reconstruct or validate the inherited slice against the referenced v34 snapshot rather than trusting the stored integrity flags.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make branch publication idempotent for receipt retries**

If the push at line 170 succeeds but the subsequent `actions/upload-artifact` step fails—for example, because of a transient artifact-service error—the permanent branch exists without the required receipts. Rerunning the workflow then stops at this nonempty-ref check before recreating or uploading either receipt, so the failed run cannot recover without manually deleting the published branch. Accept an existing ref when it already equals `CANDIDATE`, or preserve the receipts before performing the one-shot publication.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the preserved base-control contents**

When any PC-01 through PC-38 body is altered while its `control_id` remains unchanged, this validator still succeeds because it checks only the control count and ID set; the recorded `base_controls_sha256` is merely syntax-checked and never recomputed. For example, changing `controls[0].failure_class` in a compiled v37 artifact produces no validation errors, so a corrupted base floor can still be reported as preserving all thirty-eight controls.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the build checksum to the supplied fixture**

When the validator is given a valid fixture and a stale build generated from an earlier fixture revision, it validates the two independently and accepts any 64-character hexadecimal `fixture_sha256`. A still-valid change such as editing a world description therefore leaves both validators successful even though the build no longer reconstructs from the supplied fixture, defeating the checksum's source-custody purpose.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Configure an identity before invoking commit-tree**

On a clean hosted runner, this `git commit-tree` invocation exits with `Author identity unknown` unless `user.name` and `user.email` or the equivalent environment variables are configured. The same omission exists in the base, v3, and v4 materializer workflows, and their path filters all match files added by this commit, so they will produce failed workflow runs even though v5 includes the required configuration. Configure the identity in every active workflow or disable the superseded materializers.

body: Addressed with a complete exact schema contract. `validateSchemaAgainstSource` now SHA-256 binds the full stable-serialized schema before retaining the existing source-specific count and boundary checks. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Lease main in the publication transaction**

When `main` advances after the comparison on line 104 but before this push, the push still succeeds because its only lease protects `TARGET_BRANCH`; `git push -h` describes `--force-with-lease=<refname>:<expect>` as requiring the old value of that specified ref. The published product is then parented to a stale `publication_base`, and the newly merged main changes were neither overlap-checked nor tested, violating the workflow's exact-current-main guarantee. Make the main-head guard part of the atomic publication operation rather than relying on the preceding fetch-and-test.

body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin checkout to the triggering PR head**

If this branch is synchronized while an earlier run is queued, GitHub executes the earlier workflow definition but this checkout resolves the branch's newer tip; `source_head` and the subsequent lease checks therefore bind the receipt to the new commit even though the old materializer script is running. The old run can publish its obsolete package first, after which the run for the actual new workflow refuses to proceed because the one-shot target branch exists. Check out `${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}` (or otherwise compare it with the checked-out commit) so each run executes against the source revision that triggered it.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enumerate paths changed anywhere in the mainline range**

When a protected PC-44 path is changed and then restored between `SOURCE_BASE` and `publication_base`, this endpoint-tree diff omits it, so the overlap check passes and the receipt falsely claims that every intervening mainline path was enumerated. Git's documented `git diff <commit> <commit>` form compares the two endpoint trees; use the commits in the range (for example, log their changed paths) to enforce the promised historical zero-overlap invariant.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make the main-head lease atomic with publication**

If `main` advances after the final comparison on line 272 but before this push, the workflow successfully creates a target whose parent is no longer the live canonical `main`, despite the stated publication invariant. The only lease here applies to the absent target—`git push -h` describes `<refname>:<expect>` as requiring that ref's old value—so it does not protect `main`; include the expected main ref in the same atomic remote transaction or otherwise make branch creation conditional on the observed main SHA.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the v37 sources into transitive validation**

When a validator-permitted v37 source manifest is revised while previously generated v37–v42 artifacts remain on disk, this transitive call eventually bottoms out at `validatePreferenceCustodyManifestV37Build(compiled)`, which accepts no manifest or fixture. The supplied artifacts can therefore remain mutually consistent with the old source and the v42 validator will qualify the stale floor without ever reading the revised v37 source. Extend the source bundle through v37, or bind it to an explicit immutable source-aware cutoff.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the entire identification requirement**

When a revised v42 manifest deletes or replaces `identification_requirement.required_state` or `refused_inference`, validation still succeeds because only `stage` is checked. The compiler then seals that incomplete object into the promotion custody event and emits a qualified floor, allowing the manifest to lose the stated interval, dependence, multiplicity, monitoring, recalibration, and refusal boundary. Validate the full required object rather than only its stage.

Triggering this controller can leave the target branch published without its required publication receipt: the workflow force-pushes the product in `.github/workflows/temporary-ssc-rd03-qualified-publication-v1.yml` lines 173–183, then independently downloads the qualification artifact again at lines 185–205. If that artifact is deleted or becomes unavailable after the first verified download—the exact failure mode described for the previous attempt—the push has already succeeded, but receipt creation and upload fail. Preserve the initially verified receipt, path list, and manifest outside the cleaned worktree so the post-push receipt does not depend on a second artifact download.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make the main lease atomic with the target push**

When `main` advances after the `ls-remote` check in `.github/tmp/publish-rd03-qualified-v3.sh:142` but before the push at lines 146–148, this trigger publishes a product based on stale main despite the transaction's unchanged-main invariant. The checked `git push -h` semantics say `--force-with-lease=<refname>:<expect>` only requires that named ref to retain its expected value, and the command leases only the target branch; include main in an atomic push/lease transaction rather than relying on the pre-push check.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Replace the corrupted first package shard**

The committed `part-00` has SHA-256 `fc487133f9608da67b70a731124ccd412bd624260fe78b04b3761da49889df3d`, not the pinned `cd9ae320...`; moreover, concatenating the five committed shards produces a 39,285-byte Base64 stream that GNU `base64 --decode` rejects as invalid. Because the checksum verification runs under `set -e`, every workflow execution stops at `sha256sum -c` before any qualification or publication, so the shard must be replaced with the intended checksum-bound bytes rather than merely changing this hash.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep main covered by the publication lease**

If `main` advances after its early check on line 139 while the potentially two-hour qualification runs, this push can still succeed and the receipt will claim publication under the exact lease. The `git push -h` definition of `--force-with-lease[=<refname>:<expect>]` is “require old value of ref to be at this value,” and the only ref named here is the target branch, so canonical `main` is unconstrained at publication time; revalidate and protect `main` as part of the publication transaction.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Install the publication workflow before adding its trigger**

At the pinned `a7940aa8` main lease, this marker cannot trigger the intended transaction: `.github/workflows/temporary-ssc-rd03-qualified-publication-v5.yml` first appears later in `e4c25334` on this same temporary lineage, while GitHub evaluates `pull_request` workflows only when the workflow file already exists on the default branch. Conversely, advancing `main` to include that workflow makes `.github/tmp/publish-rd03-qualified-v3.sh:86` reject the run because it requires `origin/main` to remain at `a7940aa8`. Thus adding this path produces no successful publication job; use a workflow already installed on the default branch or a separately installed dispatch mechanism before committing the trigger.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enable errexit before triggering the publication controller**

When this marker starts `temporary-ssc-rd03-qualified-publication-v7.yml`, the generated child script still begins with `set -Euo pipefail`, which enables `errtrace` but omits `errexit`; invoking that executable from the action's `bash -e` shell does not propagate `-e` into the child. Consequently failures from the focused checks, `npm run release:check`, lease assertions, or even `git push` are ignored, and execution can reach the unconditional `capture_state 0`, recording a successful publication transaction despite a failed gate or push. Add `-e` to the controller's own shell options before activating it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Register the materializer workflow before triggering it**

When this trigger PR is opened while `main` remains at the required `a7940aa81b07caff1a9c2f8548c88ec37d60d676`, GitHub cannot dispatch `.github/workflows/temporary-ssc-rd03-terminal-materializer-v5.yml`: a `pull_request` workflow must exist on the default branch, but that workflow was introduced only in descendant commit `7875c9f8`. Putting the carrier commits on `main` first does not solve this, because `materialize-00.sh` then fetches the advanced `main` and rejects it against `EXPECTED_MAIN_HEAD`. Consequently this `TRIGGER` cannot start the advertised transaction; use a dispatcher already registered on the default branch or decouple registration from the pinned integration head.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the required source-head ancestry**

When this reviewed commit is checked out, its sole parent is `a7940aa8`, and `SOURCE_HEAD` (`e70aec0f`) is not an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor ... 29eafc6c` exits 1). This check therefore throws `source head is not ancestor`, so the validator invoked by the new workflow always fails for this commit; either retain the source-head merge ancestry in the submitted history or validate the preserved blob without requiring ancestry.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Narrow the promoted-order replacement before triggering**

When this trigger runs the materializer against `EXPECTED_MAIN` (`580d9c9`), `.github/tmp/materialize-ssc-rd03-ledger5.py` calls `replace_once` for `['RD-04-C01','RD-05-C03','RD-01-C03','RD-06-C01']`, but that exact text occurs twice in `tools/validate-status-sovereignty-residual-denominator-wave-02-current.mjs` (the promoted order and closed-class IDs checks). The script therefore raises `RuntimeError: promoted order: expected one match, found 2` during the workflow's `apply-exact-patch` step and never publishes the ledger branch; use a context-specific replacement for the promoted-order assertion before activating the workflow.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update the RD-03 test for the promoted ledger**

Even after correcting the earlier replacement failure, this trigger cannot complete: the generated current ledger is in `post_promotion`, but the workflow's focused qualification runs `test/status-sovereignty-rd-wave02-rd03-negotiated-terms.test.js`, whose line 8 unconditionally expects `validateCurrentAtlasCustody(bundle.current, ...)` to return `pre_promotion`. Replaying the materialization reaches this assertion and fails with actual `post_promotion` versus expected `pre_promotion`, so the test must accommodate the materialized state before this trigger can publish anything.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Derive RD-03's match flag from the labels it reports**

For RD-03, the emitted `constitutional_exact_label` and `receipt_class_label` are byte-for-byte identical, but this special case substitutes the closure's constitution-versus-seed flag and therefore records `labels_exact_match: false` and increments `label_reconciliations`. Consumers of the cumulative ledger will consequently infer two receipt/constitution mismatches even though only RD-05 has one. Preserve the seed mismatch separately, but derive this flattened flag consistently from the two labels exposed by the row.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Paid in follow-up PR #1001. The cumulative RD-03 row now derives `labels_exact_match` from its exposed constitutional and receipt labels (`true`) and records row-level `label_reconciliation: none`; the cumulative reconciliation count is 1, leaving RD-05 as the sole flattened mismatch. RD-03’s separate constitution-versus-seed mismatch remains enforced in the closure receipt. Exact product: `95452a202818bf32dfea07a5ee5396a933e7bf49`, tree `1b6e1d9e37aaa372f2e917d341a0513bf3b985f7`; qualification run `30881839025` passed 44 cumulative, 95 RD-03, and 110 RD-06 refusal mutations, the complete release gate, and deterministic replay.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Replace the malformed carrier before triggering materialization**

When this trigger starts the `Reconstruct and execute checksum-bound terminal carrier` step, the checksum-approved ZIP cannot be extracted successfully: testing the exact three carrier blobs with `unzip -t` reports `file #4: bad zipfile offset (local header sig): 5571` and exits with status 2, while the documented `-t` operation tests compressed archive data. The workflow runs `unzip -q` under `set -Eeuo pipefail`, so it exits before `materialize.sh` is invoked (and the missing entry is the terminal test file), preventing this execution-only commit from producing the branch or receipt it exists to create.

This check fails on every run because the committed `product.b64.part-00` hashes to `fcd8fca1a59ceaf6f804535b6c8399b924ab4c53134aa61d31e31ca455cdde16`, not the listed `d8e810...`; it also contains 12,001 Base64 characters, making the concatenated transport length invalid. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Correct the authored shard before triggering materialization**

When this trigger activates `.github/workflows/temporary-ssc-rd02-terminal-materializer-v2.yml`, the transaction exits before creating the product branch: the checked-in `.rd02-terminal-v2/authored/part-01.b64` hashes to `12d93451948d2918c64ea39e2e8e5b891d9d57b5c795276740295a7f1c3bc881`, while the checksum-bound executor requires `61f2305cd01758e4b8a795eb172a87f71763eba564d107ef1980c2ca24229df9` at executor line 163. Consequently the aggregate archive is also invalid and fails `gzip -t`, so the sole effect of this commit is to launch a deterministically failing materializer; replace the corrupted shard or regenerate the executor checksums before adding the trigger.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard CLI execution from module imports**

When the validator or adversarial test imports this builder, `process.argv[2]` is normally absent, so this top-level code selects `--write` and regenerates the tracked terminal products before validation. As a result, invoking either `node tools/validate-status-sovereignty-rd-wave02-rd02-license-leverage.mjs` or the corresponding test can silently repair drift and then pass instead of reporting it; only execute the write/check modes when this file is the direct entry point.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run and trigger the field-matrix checks**

The workflow covers only the terminal builder, validator, and test, while this commit also adds the RD-02 acquisition builder/validator and `status-sovereignty-rd-wave02-rd02-field-matrix.test.js`. Those files are also absent from the workflow path filters and from `npm test`, so a PR changing only the acquisition implementation will skip this workflow entirely, and the new adversarial field-matrix suite is never exercised even when the workflow runs.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Freeze the standalone interpretation contract**

When a revised fixture changes `interpretation_contract.what_this_is` or its copy-ready caveat to assert a real identity, interval, coverage, or authority claim, this validator still returns success because it validates the refusal and classification ledgers but never checks the interpretation contract. The compiler copies that arbitrary contract into the qualified standalone artifact, and the v44 compiler will consequently admit and hash it as a valid PC-46 source, so the permanent gates do not enforce the stated no-real-world-claim boundary.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject contradictory per-world burden assignments**

When defect counts are redistributed between worlds while preserving their aggregate totals—for example, assigning all 100 `undefined_event_pairs` to the complete-assurance world and zero to the undefined-event world—validation and deterministic build validation both still pass. `classifyWorld` considers only the booleans, while this loop checks only nonnegativity and later aggregate sums, producing a qualified world that simultaneously has complete target-event assurance and 100 undefined events; enforce the expected burden/state relationship within each world rather than only across the fixture.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject unrecognized fields before copying worlds**

When a fixture revision adds an unrecognized world property such as `controller` or `causal_finding`, the fixture validator ignores it and this spread copies it into the qualified PC-46 artifact; deterministic build validation then reconstructs the same tainted output and still succeeds. This allows explicitly forbidden real-world fields to coexist with classifications such as `real_world_effect_claimed: false`, so reject extra world keys or project only the approved schema before compilation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore exact current-result custody checks**

When the RD-06 workflow validates a successor ledger, this predicate never compares `current_result.classes_closed`, `classes_open`, `closed_class_ids`, or `open_selected_class_ids`; the rewritten historical predicates also dropped those comparisons. Consequently, a ledger whose top-level counts say 6/36 but whose `current_result` says 999/-957 with no closed IDs still returns `post_rd02_promotion`, so the dedicated custody gate no longer proves an internally consistent ledger. Restore the expected result fields for every accepted custody world.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind each declared unit to its frozen value**

The validator only requires `declared_unit` to be a nonempty string, so an execution branch can replace a frozen denominator such as all eighteen cohort rows with any other nonempty scope while retaining the expected count and still pass both focused checks. Since these strings define which records must be terminally classified, compare each value with an exact entry in `EXPECTED_ATTEMPTS` rather than checking presence alone.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Freeze the required closure conditions**

Only the array length is checked here, and the schema likewise accepts any six nonempty strings. Replacing the six custody and adversarial requirements with arbitrary text therefore passes the validator, allowing later receipts to claim compliance against a weakened closure contract; compare the complete ordered condition list with frozen expected values.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply the closed schema to the constitution value**

`validateConstitutionData` inspects selected schema attributes and handpicked value fields but never validates `value` against `schema`. Consequently schema-invalid mutations such as replacing `boundaries` with `{}` or adding unsupported properties pass this call despite the schema's `required` and `additionalProperties: false` contracts, so the workflow can report a structurally invalid constitution as valid.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

When this push succeeds but any later receipt construction or the upload-artifact step fails, the target branch has already been published while the required materialization receipt is lost. Because the workflow also rejects reruns once `TARGET_BRANCH` exists, a transient post-push failure leaves the carrier unable to reproduce and retain the receipt without manual branch deletion; move the push after the receipt is safely preserved or make reruns idempotent for the already-pushed commit.

Because this pushes the target branch before the receipt is generated and uploaded, any later failure in receipt creation or `actions/upload-artifact` leaves `refs/heads/$TARGET_BRANCH` present without the custody artifact this materializer promises to preserve. A rerun then hits the branch-absence guard just above and exits before it can recreate/upload the receipt, so a transient post-push failure becomes unrecoverable without manual cleanup; push only after the artifact is safely preserved, or allow reruns when the existing branch matches the computed commit.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail capture when required PDF routes do not capture PDFs**

The final guard only verifies that two receipts exist, so any transport failure, non-200 response, disallowed redirect, or non-PDF body still lets the workflow succeed and upload an artifact even though the protocol marks PDF magic as required for success. In the current DL002 malformed-URL case this would publish a two-route artifact with one failed route instead of failing the capture job, so the guard should also require each receipt to be `http_success_pdf_captured_text_inspection_pending`/`is_pdf_magic`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the v45 base build before promotion**

When a supplied v45 `baseBuild` is self-consistently altered outside the few fields checked here (for example `status`, `graph_effect`, thesis/conclusion flags, custody-chain hashes, or promotion contents), `compilePreferenceCustodyManifestV46` still accepts and hashes that unqualified floor as the v46 parent because this path never runs the existing full v45 build validator against `baseSources`. Please validate the complete v45 build before treating it as qualified lineage.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject extra keys in all transitive source bundles**

When a caller supplies a self-consistent v45 lineage with an extra key below the immediate v44 bundle, for example `baseSources.baseSources.baseSources.controller` on the v43 source bundle, recompiled v45 and v46 builds are accepted with zero validation errors. This only seals the top v45 bundle and the immediate v44 bundle shape, so deeper transitive source bundles can carry unrecognized content while still producing a qualified v46 floor; add recursive exact-key validation for every transitive source bundle before hashing/compilation.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin the manifest file's byte hash**

When only `manager-lineage-replay-manifest.json` is reformatted but its JSON values stay the same, this check still passes because `canonicalJsonSha(manifest)` hashes the parsed object after normalizing it. That lets the validator accept a manifest file whose actual SHA-256 no longer matches the documented/expected `manifestSha`, weakening the exact-byte custody claim for the package; compare the raw manifest file bytes to `EXPECTED.manifestSha` before parsing or alongside this semantic check.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Gate terminal success on source capture completion**

When any matched accession's EDGAR folder or XML fetch fails or only hashes are recorded, `filing_captures` records that non-captured state but this still marks the receipt terminal as long as the quarterly ZIPs and anchor CIKs succeeded. Since the workflow only asserts `receipt['terminal'] is True`, a run can pass and upload an artifact that is missing the required filing-folder index/XML sources for some matches; include the capture states in the terminal/failure criteria.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mirror the PR dependency paths for pushes**

In this workflow the `push.paths` filter drops several inputs that the terminal build treats as fixed custody (the seed, parent RD-02 closure/receipt tree, and Wave-03 constitution are in the PR filter but absent here). On a main push that changes only one of those upstream artifacts, GitHub will skip this workflow, so `node tools/validate-status-sovereignty-rd-wave03-rd02-portfolio-lifecycle.mjs` never gets a chance to fail the hard-coded input SHA / derivation checks and the published terminal product can remain stale. Please include the same dependency paths here as in the PR trigger.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard the lifecycle zero counters in schema checks**

`validateSchemaContract` verifies only the aggregate `lifecycle_events_observed` count before moving to `result_spawned_requests`, so a schema change that relaxes one of the event-specific constants (portfolio investments, exits, defaults, SBA repayments, etc.) still passes while the published schema no longer enforces the no-lifecycle-events boundary. Add the seven event-specific observed counters to this contract loop so schema-only mutations cannot weaken those guarantees.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recursively reject unhashable v45 base keys before cache hits**

After any previous clean compile warms `QUALIFIED_V45_BASE_VALIDATION_CACHE`, this preflight only checks the top-level `baseBuild`/`baseSources` ledgers, so a nested v45 build ledger can still be substituted with an un-JSON-serialized key such as `baseBuild.composition.controller = undefined` or a function. That mutation hashes to the same cache key because `sha256({ baseBuild, baseSources })` omits it, `validateBaseSources` does not recurse into the v45 build ledgers, and a fresh `validatePreferenceCustodyManifestV45Build` would reject it as `compiled v45 composition key ledger mismatch`; with the warmed cache, both compile and build validation accept the mutated base as qualified.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

For the IRS TEOS zip downloads, the text files are pipe-delimited records whose column order is defined externally by the IRS ([Pub 78](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-tege/pub-78-data-dictionary.pdf), [990-N](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-tege/990n-data-dictionary.pdf), [auto revocation](https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-tege/auto-revocation-data-dictionary.pdf)). Creating `DictReader` without dataset-specific `fieldnames` treats the first organization row as the header, so `sanitized_candidate()` cannot find `ORGANIZATION NAME`/`EIN` in Pub 78, 990-N, or auto-revocation, and that first raw row is later persisted in `members[*].fields`, contrary to the artifact's no-address/officer-details contract. Please provide per-dataset headers and avoid writing raw inferred headers for `zip_delimited` sources.

+def utc_now() -> str:

+        .replace("+00:00", "Z")
+    )

+def normalize_space(value: Any) -> str:
+    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(value or "")).strip()

+
+def normalize_name(value: Any) -> str:
+    text = normalize_space(value).upper().replace("&", " AND ")
+    text = re.sub(r"[^A-Z0-9]+", " ", text)
+    return normalize_space(text)

+def normalize_ein(value: Any) -> str | None:
+    digits = re.sub(r"\D", "", str(value or ""))
+    return digits if len(digits) == 9 else None

+def candidate_id(prefix: str, *parts: Any) -> str:
+    payload = "\x1f".join(normalize_space(part) for part in parts)
+    digest = hashlib.sha256(payload.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:20]
+    return f"{prefix}-{digest}"

+@dataclass
+class FetchResponse:
+    ok: bool
+    status: int | None
+    body: bytes
+    headers: dict[str, str]
+    error: str | None
+    attempts: int
+    final_url: str
+
+
+class Fetcher:
+    def __init__(self, user_agent: str, retries: int, sleep_seconds: float) -> None:
+        self.user_agent = user_agent
+        self.retries = retries
+        self.sleep_seconds = sleep_seconds
+        self.request_count = 0
+        self.opener = urllib.request.build_opener(
+            urllib.request.HTTPCookieProcessor()
+        )
+
+    def request(
+        self,
+        url: str,
+        *,
+        method: str = "GET",
+        form: dict[str, str] | None = None,
+        timeout: int = 120,
+        referer: str | None = None,
+    ) -> FetchResponse:
+        encoded = None
+        if form is not None:
+            encoded = urllib.parse.urlencode(form).encode("utf-8")
+        last_error: str | None = None
+        last_body = b""
+        last_status: int | None = None
+        last_headers: dict[str, str] = {}
+        final_url = url
+        for attempt in range(1, self.retries + 1):
+            headers = {
+                "User-Agent": self.user_agent,
+                "Accept": "text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/json,text/plain,*/*",
+                "Accept-Encoding": "identity",
+                "Connection": "close",
+            }
+            if referer:
+                headers["Referer"] = referer
+            request = urllib.request.Request(
+                url,
+                data=encoded,
+                headers=headers,
+                method=method,
+            )
+            try:
+                with self.opener.open(request, timeout=timeout) as response:
+                    body = response.read()
+                    status = int(getattr(response, "status", 200))
+                    response_headers = {
+                        key.lower(): value for key, value in response.headers.items()
+                    }
+                    final_url = response.geturl()
+                    self.request_count += 1
+                    time.sleep(self.sleep_seconds)
+                    return FetchResponse(
+                        ok=200 <= status < 400,
+                        status=status,
+                        body=body,
+                        headers=response_headers,
+                        error=None,
+                        attempts=attempt,
+                        final_url=final_url,
+                    )
+            except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
+                last_status = exc.code
+                try:
+                    last_body = exc.read()
+                except Exception:
+                    last_body = b""
+                last_headers = {
+                    key.lower(): value for key, value in exc.headers.items()
+                }
+                final_url = exc.geturl()
+                last_error = f"HTTPError: {exc.code} {exc.reason}"
+                retryable = exc.code in {408, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504}
+                if not retryable:
+                    break
+            except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as exc:
+                last_error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
+            if attempt < self.retries:
+                delay = min(20.0, 1.5 * (2 ** (attempt - 1)))
+                print(
+                    f"attempt {attempt}/{self.retries} failed for {url}: "
+                    f"{last_error}; sleep {delay:.1f}s",
+                    file=sys.stderr,
+                    flush=True,
+                )
+                time.sleep(delay)
+        return FetchResponse(
+            ok=False,
+            status=last_status,
+            body=last_body,
+            headers=last_headers,
+            error=last_error or "request_failed",
+            attempts=self.retries,
+            final_url=final_url,
+        )

+class TextParser(HTMLParser):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
+        self.parts: list[str] = []
+
+    def handle_data(self, data: str) -> None:
+        text = normalize_space(data)
+        if text:
+            self.parts.append(text)
+
+    def handle_starttag(
+        self, tag: str, attrs: list[tuple[str, str | None]]
+    ) -> None:
+        if tag.lower() in {"br", "p", "div", "tr", "li", "h1", "h2", "h3"}:
+            self.parts.append("\n")
+
+    def handle_endtag(self, tag: str) -> None:
+        if tag.lower() in {"p", "div", "tr", "li", "h1", "h2", "h3"}:
+            self.parts.append("\n")
+
+
+def html_text(body: bytes) -> str:
+    parser = TextParser()
+    parser.feed(body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
+    text = " ".join(parser.parts)
+    text = re.sub(r"[ \t]+\n", "\n", text)
+    text = re.sub(r"\n[ \t]+", "\n", text)
+    text = re.sub(r"\n{2,}", "\n", text)
+    return text.strip()
+
+
+class TableParser(HTMLParser):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
+        self.rows: list[list[dict[str, Any]]] = []
+        self.current_row: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None
+        self.current_cell: dict[str, Any] | None = None
+        self.current_link: dict[str, str] | None = None
+
+    def handle_starttag(
+        self, tag: str, attrs: list[tuple[str, str | None]]
+    ) -> None:
+        tag = tag.lower()
+        attr = {key.lower(): value or "" for key, value in attrs}
+        if tag == "tr":
+            self.current_row = []
+        elif tag in {"td", "th"} and self.current_row is not None:
+            self.current_cell = {"parts": [], "links": []}
+        elif tag == "a" and self.current_cell is not None:
+            self.current_link = {"href": attr.get("href", ""), "parts": []}
+        elif tag == "br" and self.current_cell is not None:
+            self.current_cell["parts"].append(" ")
+
+    def handle_data(self, data: str) -> None:
+        if self.current_cell is not None:
+            self.current_cell["parts"].append(data)
+        if self.current_link is not None:
+            self.current_link["parts"].append(data)
+
+    def handle_endtag(self, tag: str) -> None:
+        tag = tag.lower()
+        if tag == "a" and self.current_link is not None:
+            self.current_link["text"] = normalize_space(
+                "".join(self.current_link.pop("parts"))
+            )
+            if self.current_cell is not None:
+                self.current_cell["links"].append(self.current_link)
+            self.current_link = None
+        elif tag in {"td", "th"} and self.current_cell is not None:
+            cell = {
+                "text": normalize_space("".join(self.current_cell["parts"])),
+                "links": self.current_cell["links"],
+            }
+            if self.current_row is not None:
+                self.current_row.append(cell)
+            self.current_cell = None
+        elif tag == "tr" and self.current_row is not None:
+            if any(cell.get("text") or cell.get("links") for cell in self.current_row):
+                self.rows.append(self.current_row)
+            self.current_row = None
+

+class FormParser(HTMLParser):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
+        self.forms: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+        self.current: dict[str, Any] | None = None
+        self.current_button: dict[str, str] | None = None
+
+    def handle_starttag(
+        self, tag: str, attrs: list[tuple[str, str | None]]
+    ) -> None:
+        tag = tag.lower()
+        attr = {key.lower(): value or "" for key, value in attrs}
+        if tag == "form":
+            self.current = {
+                "action": attr.get("action", ""),
+                "method": attr.get("method", "get").upper(),
+                "inputs": [],
+                "buttons": [],
+            }
+        elif tag == "input" and self.current is not None:
+            self.current["inputs"].append(
+                {
+                    "name": attr.get("name", ""),
+                    "id": attr.get("id", ""),
+                    "type": attr.get("type", "text").lower(),
+                    "value": attr.get("value", ""),
+                }
+            )
+        elif tag == "button" and self.current is not None:
+            self.current_button = {
+                "name": attr.get("name", ""),
+                "id": attr.get("id", ""),
+                "type": attr.get("type", "submit").lower(),
+                "value": attr.get("value", ""),
+                "text": "",
+            }
+
+    def handle_data(self, data: str) -> None:
+        if self.current_button is not None:
+            self.current_button["text"] += data
+
+    def handle_endtag(self, tag: str) -> None:
+        tag = tag.lower()
+        if tag == "button" and self.current_button is not None:
+            self.current_button["text"] = normalize_space(
+                self.current_button["text"]
+            )
+            if self.current is not None:
+                self.current["buttons"].append(self.current_button)
+            self.current_button = None
+        elif tag == "form" and self.current is not None:
+            self.forms.append(self.current)
+            self.current = None
+

+def document_number(text: str) -> str | None:
+    matches = re.findall(r"\b[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{5,15}\b", text.upper())
+    for match in matches:
+        if any(char.isdigit() for char in match) and len(match) >= 7:
+            return match
+    return None

+    return None

+def line_after(text: str, label: str) -> str | None:
+    match = re.search(
+        rf"(?:^|\n){re.escape(label)}\s+([^\n]+)", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE
+    )
+    return normalize_space(match.group(1)) if match else None

+def section_lines(text: str, start: str, end_labels: list[str]) -> list[str]:
+    lines = [normalize_space(line) for line in text.splitlines() if normalize_space(line)]
+    start_index = next(
+        (index for index, line in enumerate(lines) if line.lower() == start.lower()),
+        None,
+    )
+    if start_index is None:
+        return []
+    end_index = len(lines)
+    for index in range(start_index + 1, len(lines)):
+        if any(lines[index].lower() == label.lower() for label in end_labels):
+            end_index = index
+            break
+    return lines[start_index + 1 : end_index]
+

+def city_state_from_principal(text: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
+    lines = section_lines(
+        text,
+        "Principal Address",
+        [
+            "Mailing Address",
+            "Registered Agent Name & Address",
+            "Officer/Director Detail",
+            "Authorized Person(s) Detail",
+            "Annual Reports",
+        ],
+    )
+    for line in reversed(lines):
+        match = re.search(
+            r"^(.+?),\s*([A-Z]{2})(?:\s+\d{5}(?:-\d{4})?)?(?:\s+.*)?$",
+            line.upper(),
+        )
+        if match:
+            return normalize_space(match.group(1)), match.group(2)
+    return None, None
+
