+def parse_sunbiz_detail(body: bytes, source_url: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+    text = html_text(body)
+    if "Filing Information" not in text:
+        return None
+    lines = [normalize_space(line) for line in text.splitlines() if normalize_space(line)]
+    filing_index = next(
+        (index for index, line in enumerate(lines) if line == "Filing Information"),
+        None,
+    )
+    legal_name = None
+    filing_type = None
+    if filing_index is not None:
+        preceding = [
+            line
+            for line in lines[max(0, filing_index - 5) : filing_index]
+            if not line.lower().startswith("detail by")
+        ]
+        if preceding:
+            legal_name = preceding[-1]
+        if len(preceding) >= 2:
+            filing_type = preceding[-2]
+    joined = "\n".join(lines)
+    doc_match = re.search(r"Document Number\s+([A-Z0-9]+)", joined, re.I)
+    fei_match = re.search(r"FEI/EIN Number\s+([A-Z0-9\-]+)", joined, re.I)
+    date_match = re.search(r"Date Filed\s+([0-9/\-]+)", joined, re.I)
+    state_match = re.search(r"\bState\s+([A-Z]{2})\b", joined, re.I)
+    status_match = re.search(r"\bStatus\s+([A-Z /-]+?)(?:\s+Last Event|\n|$)", joined, re.I)
+    city, state = city_state_from_principal(joined)
+    officer_section = section_lines(
+        joined,
+        "Officer/Director Detail Name & Address",
+        ["Annual Reports", "Document Images"],
+    )
+    if not officer_section:
+        officer_section = section_lines(
+            joined,
+            "Authorized Person(s) Detail Name & Address",
+            ["Annual Reports", "Document Images"],
+        )
+    officer_count = sum(1 for line in officer_section if line.startswith("Title"))
+    return {
+        "legal_name": legal_name,
+        "normalized_name": normalize_name(legal_name),
+        "document_number": doc_match.group(1) if doc_match else None,
+        "registration_number": None,
+        "status": normalize_space(status_match.group(1)) if status_match else None,
+        "filing_type": filing_type,
+        "date_filed": date_match.group(1) if date_match else None,

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Decode timeout stderr before appending text**

When any of the 204 curl requests exceeds the subprocess timeout, `TimeoutExpired.stderr`/`stdout` are bytes even though `subprocess.run(..., text=True)` was used; this concatenation can raise `TypeError: can't concat str to bytes` before the route receipt is written. That turns a single slow route, which the runner intends to record as `terminal_transport_failure`, into a failed capture job with incomplete artifacts.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid comparing main pushes against origin/main**

The workflow added in `.github/workflows/status-sovereignty-rd-wave03-rd04-state-implementation-intake.yml` runs this validator on `push` to `main` after `actions/checkout@v4` with `fetch-depth: 0`; in that context `origin/main` is the pushed commit, so selecting it here makes `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` empty and the next denominator check fails as `0/11` on the merge-to-main run. Use the fixed design base or the event's pre-push/base SHA for push validation instead of the remote branch tip.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

+def utc_now() -> str:
+    return (
+        datetime.now(timezone.utc)
+        .replace(microsecond=0)
+        .isoformat()
+        .replace("+00:00", "Z")
+    )

+def normalize_space(value: Any) -> str:
+    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(value or "")).strip()
+
+
+def normalize_name(value: Any) -> str:
+    text = normalize_space(value).upper().replace("&", " AND ")
+    text = re.sub(r"[^A-Z0-9]+", " ", text)
+    return normalize_space(text)
+
+
+def normalize_ein(value: Any) -> str | None:
+    digits = re.sub(r"\D", "", str(value or ""))
+    return digits if len(digits) == 9 else None

+
+def normalize_document(value: Any) -> str | None:
+    text = re.sub(r"[^A-Z0-9]", "", str(value or "").upper())
+    return text or None

+def sha256_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

+def compact(value: Any) -> str:
+    return json.dumps(
+        value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
+    )

+def read_json(path: Path) -> Any:

+def read_jsonl(path: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+    for number, line in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), 1):
+        if not line.strip():
+            continue
+        try:
+            rows.append(json.loads(line))
+        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"{path}:{number}: {exc}") from exc
+    return rows

+def write_json(path: Path, value: Any) -> None:
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text(
+        json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n",
+        encoding="utf-8",
+    )

+def write_jsonl(path: Path, rows: Iterable[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as handle:
+        for row in rows:

+def stable_id(prefix: str, *values: Any) -> str:
+    payload = "\x1f".join(normalize_space(value) for value in values)
+    return f"{prefix}-{sha256_bytes(payload.encode('utf-8'))[:20]}"

+@dataclass
+class FetchResponse:
+    ok: bool
+    status: int | None
+    body: bytes
+    headers: dict[str, str]
+    error: str | None
+    attempts: int
+    final_url: str
+
+
+class Fetcher:
+    def __init__(self, user_agent: str, retries: int, sleep_seconds: float) -> None:
+        self.user_agent = user_agent
+        self.retries = retries
+        self.sleep_seconds = sleep_seconds
+        self.request_count = 0
+        self.opener = urllib.request.build_opener(
+            urllib.request.HTTPCookieProcessor()
+        )
+
+    def request(
+        self,
+        url: str,
+        *,
+        method: str = "GET",
+        form: dict[str, str] | None = None,
+        referer: str | None = None,
+        timeout: int = 45,
+    ) -> FetchResponse:
+        data = (
+            urllib.parse.urlencode(form).encode("utf-8")
+            if form is not None
+            else None
+        )
+        last_status: int | None = None
+        last_body = b""
+        last_headers: dict[str, str] = {}
+        last_error: str | None = None
+        final_url = url
+        for attempt in range(1, self.retries + 1):
+            headers = {
+                "User-Agent": self.user_agent,
+                "Accept": "text/html,application/xhtml+xml,text/plain,*/*",
+                "Accept-Encoding": "identity",
+                "Connection": "close",
+            }
+            if referer:
+                headers["Referer"] = referer
+            request = urllib.request.Request(
+                url, data=data, headers=headers, method=method
+            )
+            try:
+                with self.opener.open(request, timeout=timeout) as response:
+                    body = response.read()
+                    status = int(getattr(response, "status", 200))
+                    response_headers = {
+                        key.lower(): value for key, value in response.headers.items()
+                    }
+                    final_url = response.geturl()
+                    self.request_count += 1
+                    time.sleep(self.sleep_seconds)
+                    return FetchResponse(
+                        ok=200 <= status < 400,
+                        status=status,
+                        body=body,
+                        headers=response_headers,
+                        error=None,
+                        attempts=attempt,
+                        final_url=final_url,
+                    )
+            except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
+                last_status = exc.code
+                try:
+                    last_body = exc.read()
+                except Exception:
+                    last_body = b""
+                last_headers = {
+                    key.lower(): value for key, value in exc.headers.items()
+                }
+                last_error = f"HTTPError: {exc.code} {exc.reason}"
+                final_url = exc.geturl()
+                if exc.code not in {408, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504}:
+                    break
+            except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as exc:
+                last_error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
+            if attempt < self.retries:
+                delay = min(20.0, 1.5 * (2 ** (attempt - 1)))
+                print(
+                    f"attempt {attempt}/{self.retries} failed for {url}: "
+                    f"{last_error}; sleep {delay:.1f}s",
+                    file=sys.stderr,
+                    flush=True,
+                )
+                time.sleep(delay)
+        return FetchResponse(
+            ok=False,
+            status=last_status,
+            body=last_body,
+            headers=last_headers,
+            error=last_error or "request_failed",
+            attempts=self.retries,
+            final_url=final_url,
+        )
+

+class TextParser(HTMLParser):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
+        self.parts: list[str] = []
+
+    def handle_starttag(
+        self, tag: str, attrs: list[tuple[str, str | None]]
+    ) -> None:
+        if tag.lower() in {
+            "br",
+            "p",
+            "div",
+            "tr",
+            "li",
+            "h1",
+            "h2",
+            "h3",
+            "section",
+        }:
+            self.parts.append("\n")
+
+    def handle_endtag(self, tag: str) -> None:
+        if tag.lower() in {
+            "p",
+            "div",
+            "tr",
+            "li",
+            "h1",
+            "h2",
+            "h3",
+            "section",
+        }:
+            self.parts.append("\n")
+
+    def handle_data(self, data: str) -> None:
+        if data:
+            self.parts.append(data)
+
+
+class LinkParser(HTMLParser):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
+        self.links: list[dict[str, str]] = []
+        self.current: dict[str, Any] | None = None
+
+    def handle_starttag(
+        self, tag: str, attrs: list[tuple[str, str | None]]
+    ) -> None:
+        if tag.lower() != "a":
+            return
+        attr = {key.lower(): value or "" for key, value in attrs}
+        self.current = {"href": attr.get("href", ""), "parts": []}
+
+    def handle_data(self, data: str) -> None:
+        if self.current is not None:
+            self.current["parts"].append(data)
+
+    def handle_endtag(self, tag: str) -> None:
+        if tag.lower() == "a" and self.current is not None:
+            self.links.append(
+                {
+                    "href": self.current["href"],
+                    "text": normalize_space("".join(self.current["parts"])),
+                }
+            )
+            self.current = None
+

+class FormParser(HTMLParser):

+                {
+                    "name": attr.get("name", ""),
+                    "id": attr.get("id", ""),
+                    "type": attr.get("type", "text").lower(),
+                    "value": attr.get("value", ""),
+                }
+            )
+        elif tag == "button" and self.current is not None:
+            self.button = {
+                "name": attr.get("name", ""),
+                "id": attr.get("id", ""),
+                "type": attr.get("type", "submit").lower(),
+                "value": attr.get("value", ""),
+                "parts": [],
+            }
+
+    def handle_data(self, data: str) -> None:
+        if self.button is not None:
+            self.button["parts"].append(data)
+
+    def handle_endtag(self, tag: str) -> None:
+        tag = tag.lower()
+        if tag == "button" and self.button is not None:
+            self.button["text"] = normalize_space(
+                "".join(self.button.pop("parts"))
+            )
+            if self.current is not None:
+                self.current["buttons"].append(self.button)
+            self.button = None
+        elif tag == "form" and self.current is not None:
+            self.forms.append(self.current)
+            self.current = None

+def html_text(body: bytes) -> str:
+    parser = TextParser()
+    parser.feed(body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
+    text = "".join(parser.parts)
+    text = html.unescape(text)
+    text = re.sub(r"\r\n?", "\n", text)
+    text = re.sub(r"[ \t]+", " ", text)
+    text = re.sub(r" *\n *", "\n", text)
+    text = re.sub(r"\n{2,}", "\n", text)
+    return text.strip()
+
+
+def links(body: bytes) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
+    parser = LinkParser()
+    parser.feed(body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
+    return parser.links
+
+
+def forms(body: bytes) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    parser = FormParser()
+    parser.feed(body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
+    return parser.forms

+def section_lines(text: str, start: str, end_labels: list[str]) -> list[str]:
+    lines = [normalize_space(line) for line in text.splitlines() if normalize_space(line)]
+    start_index = next(
+        (index for index, line in enumerate(lines) if line.lower() == start.lower()),
+        None,
+    )
+    if start_index is None:
+        return []
+    end_index = len(lines)
+    for index in range(start_index + 1, len(lines)):
+        if any(lines[index].lower() == label.lower() for label in end_labels):
+            end_index = index
+            break
+    return lines[start_index + 1 : end_index]
+

+def parse_city_state(text: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
+    principal = section_lines(
+        text,
+        "Principal Address",
+        [
+            "Mailing Address",
+            "Registered Agent Name & Address",
+            "Officer/Director Detail Name & Address",
+            "Authorized Person(s) Detail Name & Address",
+            "Annual Reports",
+            "Document Images",
+        ],
+    )
+    for line in reversed(principal):
+        match = re.search(
+            r"^(.+?),\s*([A-Z]{2})(?:\s+\d{5}(?:-\d{4})?)?(?:\s+.*)?$",
+            line.upper(),
+        )
+        if match:
+            return normalize_space(match.group(1)), match.group(2)
+    return None, None
+
+
+def parse_detail(body: bytes, source_url: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+    text = html_text(body)
+    if "Filing Information" not in text or "Document Number" not in text:
+        return None
+    lines = [normalize_space(line) for line in text.splitlines() if normalize_space(line)]
+    filing_index = next(
+        (index for index, line in enumerate(lines) if line == "Filing Information"),
+        None,
+    )
+    legal_name = None
+    entity_type = None
+    if filing_index is not None:
+        preceding = []
+        for line in lines[max(0, filing_index - 8) : filing_index]:
+            if line.lower().startswith("detail by"):
+                continue
+            if line in {
+                "Florida Department of State",
+                "Division of Corporations",
+            }:
+                continue
+            preceding.append(line)
+        if preceding:
+            legal_name = preceding[-1]
+        if len(preceding) >= 2:
+            entity_type = preceding[-2]
+    joined = "\n".join(lines)
+    document_match = re.search(r"Document Number\s+([A-Z0-9]+)", joined, re.I)
+    fei_match = re.search(r"FEI/EIN Number\s+([A-Z0-9\-]+)", joined, re.I)
+    date_match = re.search(r"Date Filed\s+([0-9/\-]+)", joined, re.I)
+    state_match = re.search(r"\bState\s+([A-Z]{2})\b", joined, re.I)
+    status_match = re.search(
+        r"\bStatus\s+([A-Z /-]+?)(?:\s+Last Event|\n|$)",
+        joined,
+        re.I,
+    )
+    city, principal_state = parse_city_state(joined)
+    officer_lines = section_lines(
+        joined,
+        "Officer/Director Detail Name & Address",
+        ["Annual Reports", "Document Images"],
+    )
+    if not officer_lines:
+        officer_lines = section_lines(
+            joined,
+            "Authorized Person(s) Detail Name & Address",
+            ["Annual Reports", "Document Images"],
+        )
+    officer_count = sum(1 for line in officer_lines if line.startswith("Title"))
+    fei_raw = normalize_space(fei_match.group(1)) if fei_match else None
+    return {
+        "source_url": source_url,
+        "legal_name_as_recorded": legal_name,
+        "normalized_legal_name": normalize_name(legal_name),
+        "document_number": (
+            normalize_document(document_match.group(1)) if document_match else None
+        ),
+        "entity_type": entity_type,
+        "status": normalize_space(status_match.group(1)) if status_match else None,
+        "date_filed": date_match.group(1) if date_match else None,
+        "state": state_match.group(1).upper() if state_match else None,
+        "fei_ein": normalize_ein(fei_raw),
+        "fei_field_state": (
+            "present" if normalize_ein(fei_raw) else "none_or_unresolved"
+        ),
+        "principal_city": city,
+        "principal_state": principal_state,
+        "officer_count": officer_count,
+        "street_address_retained": False,
+        "contact_details_retained": False,
+        "registered_agent_name_retained": False,
+        "officer_names_retained": False,
+        "document_images_retained": False,
+        "private_support_rows": 0,
+        "outside_human_dependency": False,
+        "graph_effect": "none",
+        "promotes_to": "candidate_only",
+    }
+

+def select_document_form(page: bytes) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+    scored: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]] = []
+    for form in forms(page):
+        score = 0
+        for item in form.get("inputs", []):
+            haystack = f"{item.get('name', '')} {item.get('id', '')}".lower()
+            if item.get("type") in {"text", "search", ""}:
+                score += 2
+            if "document" in haystack or "search" in haystack:
+                score += 10
+        if score:
+            scored.append((score, form))
+    return max(scored, key=lambda pair: pair[0])[1] if scored else None
+

+def form_request(
+    form: dict[str, Any], document_number: str
+) -> tuple[str, str, dict[str, str]]:
+    payload: dict[str, str] = {}
+    text_fields: list[dict[str, str]] = []
+    for item in form.get("inputs", []):
+        name = item.get("name") or ""
+        if not name:
+            continue
+        input_type = (item.get("type") or "text").lower()
+        if input_type == "hidden":
+            payload[name] = item.get("value") or ""
+        elif input_type in {"text", "search", ""}:
+            text_fields.append(item)
+    query_field = None
+    for item in text_fields:
+        haystack = f"{item.get('name', '')} {item.get('id', '')}".lower()
+        if "document" in haystack or "search" in haystack:
+            query_field = item.get("name")
+            break
+    if query_field is None and text_fields:
+        query_field = text_fields[0].get("name")
+    if not query_field:
+        raise RuntimeError("document-number form query field unresolved")
+    payload[query_field] = document_number
+    submit_added = False
+    for item in form.get("inputs", []):
+        if (item.get("type") or "").lower() not in {"submit", "button"}:
+            continue
+        name = item.get("name") or ""
+        value = item.get("value") or ""
+        if name and ("search" in value.lower() or not submit_added):
+            payload[name] = value or "Search"
+            submit_added = True
+            if "search" in value.lower():
+                break
+    if not submit_added:
+        for button in form.get("buttons", []):
+            name = button.get("name") or ""
+            value = button.get("value") or button.get("text") or "Search"
+            if name:
+                payload[name] = value
+                break
+    action = urllib.parse.urljoin(BY_DOCUMENT_NUMBER, form.get("action") or "")
+    method = form.get("method") or "POST"
+    return action, method, payload
+

+def exact_detail_link(body: bytes, base_url: str, document_number: str) -> str | None:
+    expected = normalize_document(document_number)
+    candidates = []
+    for link in links(body):
+        href = link.get("href") or ""
+        if "SearchResultDetail" not in href:
+            continue
+        resolved = urllib.parse.urljoin(base_url, href)
+        haystack = normalize_document(
+            f"{link.get('text', '')} {href}"
+        ) or ""
+        score = 2 if expected and expected in haystack else 1
+        candidates.append((score, resolved))
+    if not candidates:
+        return None
+    candidates.sort(key=lambda item: item[0], reverse=True)
+    return candidates[0][1]
+

+def fetch_document(
+    fetcher: Fetcher,
+    document_number: str,
+    form: dict[str, Any] | None,
+) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any] | None]:
+    expected = normalize_document(document_number)
+    route: dict[str, Any] = {
+        "route_id": stable_id("fl-corporate-document", expected),
+        "jurisdiction": "Florida",
+        "source_family": "fl_sunbiz_corporate_detail",
+        "query_type": "exact_document_number",
+        "query": expected,
+        "state": "not_attempted",
+        "retrieved_at": utc_now(),
+        "transport_attempts": [],
+        "raw_source_retained": False,
+        "street_address_retained": False,
+        "contact_details_retained": False,
+        "registered_agent_name_retained": False,
+        "officer_names_retained": False,
+        "document_images_retained": False,
+        "private_support_rows": 0,
+        "outside_human_dependency": False,
+        "negative_existence_claim_permitted": False,
+        "graph_effect": "none",
+        "promotes_to": "candidate_only",
+    }
+    responses: list[tuple[str, FetchResponse]] = []
+
+    path_url = (
+        f"{CORPORATE_SEARCH_BASE}/SearchResults/DocumentNumber/"
+        f"{urllib.parse.quote(expected or '', safe='')}/Page1"
+    )
+    response = fetcher.request(path_url)
+    responses.append(("path_document_search", response))
+
+    if not response.ok:
+        query_url = (
+            f"{CORPORATE_SEARCH_BASE}/SearchResults?"
+            + urllib.parse.urlencode(
+                {"inquiryType": "DocumentNumber", "searchTerm": expected or ""}
+            )
+        )
+        query_response = fetcher.request(query_url, referer=BY_DOCUMENT_NUMBER)
+        responses.append(("query_document_search", query_response))
+        if query_response.ok:
+            response = query_response
+
+    if not response.ok and form is not None:
+        try:
+            action, method, payload = form_request(form, expected or "")
+            form_response = fetcher.request(
+                action,
+                method=method,
+                form=payload,
+                referer=BY_DOCUMENT_NUMBER,
+            )
+            responses.append(("form_document_search", form_response))
+            if form_response.ok:
+                response = form_response
+        except Exception as exc:
+            route["form_error"] = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
+
+    for variant, item in responses:
+        route["transport_attempts"].append(
+            {
+                "variant": variant,
+                "requested_url": item.final_url,
+                "http_status": item.status,
+                "bytes": len(item.body),
+                "sha256": sha256_bytes(item.body),
+                "attempts": item.attempts,
+                "error": item.error,
+            }
+        )
+
+    if not response.ok:
+        route["state"] = "source_unavailable_after_search"
+        route["terminal_http_status"] = response.status
+        route["terminal_error"] = response.error
+        return route, None
+
+    search_text = html_text(response.body)
+    route["search_result_url"] = response.final_url
+    route["search_result_bytes"] = len(response.body)
+    route["search_result_sha256"] = sha256_bytes(response.body)
+    route["search_http_status"] = response.status
+
+    detail = parse_detail(response.body, response.final_url)
+    detail_response = response
+    detail_url = response.final_url
+    if detail is None:
+        if "Record Not Found" in search_text:
+            route["state"] = "document_not_found"
+            return route, None
+        link = exact_detail_link(response.body, response.final_url, expected or "")
+        if not link:
+            route["state"] = "detail_unparsed"
+            route["detail_link_resolved"] = False
+            return route, None
+        detail_url = link
+        detail_response = fetcher.request(link, referer=response.final_url)
+        route["detail_link_resolved"] = True
+        route["detail_url"] = link
+        route["detail_http_status"] = detail_response.status
+        route["detail_bytes"] = len(detail_response.body)
+        route["detail_sha256"] = sha256_bytes(detail_response.body)
+        route["detail_attempts"] = detail_response.attempts
+        if not detail_response.ok:
+            route["state"] = "source_unavailable_after_search"

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Skip mismatched details when building records**

When Sunbiz returns a detail page whose parsed Document Number does not match the queried document (for example, if the result-link heuristic lands on a neighboring row or the document field is unparsed), `fetch_document` marks the route as `document_mismatch` but still returns the detail. This block then classifies and appends that detail anyway; because `classify_record` stamps the queried document number, the later `resolved_documents`/Magnolia checks can count data from the wrong corporation as a resolved exact record. Gate record creation on `route['state'] == 'resolved_exact_document'` or discard details on mismatches.

When a target record starts in the last ~1.4 KB of a zip member, this call never sees it: the third argument to `bytes.find` is an exclusive slice end, so the 12-byte document number must be fully contained before `safe_limit`, not merely start before it. Chunk overlap recovers this for non-final chunks, but at EOF (including a one-record member or a target in the last fixed-width record) the scanner reports the exact document as missing even though the full 1,440-byte record is present.

+            value = values.get("value")
+            control: dict[str, Any] = {
+                "tag": tag,
+                "type": control_type,
+                "name": normalize_space(values.get("name")) or None,
+                "id": normalize_space(values.get("id")) or None,
+                "autocomplete": normalize_space(values.get("autocomplete")) or None,
+                "required": "required" in values,
+            }
+            if control_type == "hidden":
+                control["hidden_value_receipt"] = header_value_hash(value)
+            elif control_type in {"submit", "button", "reset"} and value is not None:
+                control["button_value"] = normalize_space(value)[:200]
+            if self.current_form is not None:
+                self.current_form["controls"].append(control)

+            href = normalize_url(self.base_url, values.get("href") or "")
+            if href:
+                self.current_anchor = {
+                    "href": href,
+                    "id": normalize_space(values.get("id")) or None,
+                    "class": normalize_space(values.get("class")) or None,
+                    "text_parts": [],
+                }
+        elif tag == "script":
+            src = normalize_url(self.base_url, values.get("src") or "")
+            if src:
+                self.scripts.append(src)
+            else:
+                self.inline_script_depth += 1
+        elif tag == "link":
+            rel = normalize_space(values.get("rel")).lower()
+            href = normalize_url(self.base_url, values.get("href") or "")
+            if href and "stylesheet" in rel:
+                self.stylesheets.append(href)
+
+    def handle_endtag(self, tag: str) -> None:
+        tag = tag.lower()
+        if tag == "title" and self.title_depth:
+            self.title_depth -= 1
+        elif tag == "form":
+            self.current_form = None
+        elif tag == "a" and self.current_anchor is not None:
+            anchor = dict(self.current_anchor)
+            anchor["text"] = normalize_space(" ".join(anchor.pop("text_parts")))[:500]

+            self.current_anchor = None
+        elif tag == "script" and self.inline_script_depth:
+            self.inline_script_depth -= 1
+

+        if self.title_depth:
+            self.title_parts.append(data)
+        if self.current_anchor is not None:
+            self.current_anchor["text_parts"].append(data)
+        if self.inline_script_depth:
+            self.inline_script_parts.append(data)
+
+    def result(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        deduped_anchors: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+        seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
+        for anchor in self.anchors:
+            key = (anchor["href"], anchor.get("text") or "")
+            if key not in seen:
+                seen.add(key)
+                deduped_anchors.append(anchor)
+        return {
+            "title": normalize_space(" ".join(self.title_parts)) or None,
+            "forms": self.forms,
+            "anchors": deduped_anchors,
+            "scripts": sorted(set(self.scripts)),
+            "stylesheets": sorted(set(self.stylesheets)),
+            "inline_script": "\n".join(self.inline_script_parts),

+def parse_header_blocks(path: Path) -> tuple[int | None, dict[str, str], list[str]]:
+    if not path.exists():
+        return None, {}, []
+    text = path.read_text(encoding="latin-1", errors="replace")
+    blocks = re.split(r"\r?\n\r?\n", text)
+    status: int | None = None
+    headers: dict[str, str] = {}
+    cookie_names: list[str] = []
+    for block in blocks:
+        lines = [line for line in block.splitlines() if line.strip()]
+        if not lines or not lines[0].startswith("HTTP/"):
+            continue
+        match = re.match(r"HTTP/\S+\s+(\d{3})", lines[0])
+        if match:
+            status = int(match.group(1))
+        current: dict[str, str] = {}
+        for line in lines[1:]:
+            if ":" not in line:
+                continue
+            key, value = line.split(":", 1)
+            key = key.strip().lower()
+            value = value.strip()
+            if key == "set-cookie":
+                name = value.split("=", 1)[0].strip()
+                if name and name not in cookie_names:
+                    cookie_names.append(name)
+            elif key in current:
+                current[key] = f"{current[key]}, {value}"
+            else:
+                current[key] = value
+        headers = current
+    return status, headers, cookie_names
+
+
+def curl_version() -> dict[str, Any]:
+    try:
+        completed = subprocess.run(
+            ["curl", "--version"],
+            check=False,
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+            timeout=15,
+        )
+    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
+        return {"available": False, "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"}
+    protocols: list[str] = []
+    features: list[str] = []
+    for line in completed.stdout.splitlines():
+        if line.startswith("Protocols:"):
+            protocols = line.split(":", 1)[1].strip().split()
+        elif line.startswith("Features:"):
+            features = line.split(":", 1)[1].strip().split()
+    return {
+        "available": completed.returncode == 0,
+        "version_line": completed.stdout.splitlines()[0] if completed.stdout else None,
+        "protocols": protocols,
+        "features": features,
+        "stderr": normalize_space(completed.stderr) or None,
+    }
+
+
+def classify_state(
+    status: int | None,
+    content_type: str,
+    returncode: int,
+    method: str,
+    body_bytes: int,
+    body_limit: int,
+) -> str:
+    if returncode == 28:
+        return "timeout"
+    if status == 401:
+        return "auth_required"
+    if status == 403:
+        return "provider_blocked"
+    if status == 404:
+        return "not_found"
+    if status is not None and status >= 500:
+        return "server_error"
+    if returncode == 63:
+        return "oversized_html_guarded" if method == "GET_HTML" else "range_guard_refused_full_body"
+    if status is None:
+        return "transport_error"
+    if status < 200 or status >= 400:
+        return "transport_error"
+    if method == "GET_RANGE":
+        return "accessible_file_sample"
+    if "text/html" in content_type.lower() or "application/xhtml" in content_type.lower():
+        return "accessible_html"
+    return "accessible_non_html" if body_bytes <= body_limit else "transport_error"

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update stale second-level validator counts**

When this workflow reaches the BVVC validator after the generated builder runs, the product has already raised `manifest.counts.source_inventory_rows` to 275 and coverage denominators to 21, but the decoded builder only appends a new final-residual validation block and leaves the existing second-level validator checks in `tools/validate-bvvc-defense-capital.mjs` asserting the old 224/20 totals. As a result, the intended materialization always reports the second-level denominator drift here and stops before committing or pushing the product branch.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare fallback surface against this commit's base**

When the validator runs in a checkout that does not have `origin/main` (for example an exported or local clone), this fallback compares `HEAD` to `3c181d6...` instead of the actual current-main/parent baseline, so `git diff --name-only` includes unrelated paths merged after that older candidate commit and `classifyChangedPathSurface` rejects the otherwise valid 14-path product. This makes the new validation command fail outside environments that happen to have `origin/main`; the fallback should use the current design/main base (or the product commit's parent) rather than the older candidate merge.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject or clear existing output directories**

When `--output` points at a directory from a previous run, this only creates the directory and then overwrites the files it happens to write in the current mode, leaving stale `routes/`, old manifests, or candidate files beside the new receipt. That makes the artifact tree disagree with the newly emitted capture manifest/receipt and can corrupt exact custody for reruns; fail if the output exists or remove it before writing.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require file samples to match successful routes**

When a final-residual file-sample row is accidentally attached to any other file-target route, for example the PDF 404 route, while one of the 15 `http_success_file_sample` routes is missing from this file, this still passes because it only checks the input link and the sample row's self-reported status; it never joins back to `finalResidualRoutes` to verify the same `route_id`/`receipt_id`/`url` and `terminal_state`. That lets corrupted custody overstate which PDFs were actually sampled.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

+def normalize_url(base_url: str, href: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:

+        return None
+    absolute = urllib.parse.urljoin(base_url, href)
+    parsed = urllib.parse.urlsplit(absolute)
+    if parsed.scheme.lower() not in {"http", "https"}:
+        return None
+    host = (parsed.hostname or "").lower()
+    path = parsed.path or "/"
+    no_query = urllib.parse.urlunsplit((parsed.scheme.lower(), parsed.netloc.lower(), path, "", ""))
+    return {
+        "absolute_url": urllib.parse.urlunsplit((parsed.scheme.lower(), parsed.netloc.lower(), path, parsed.query, "")),
+        "url_without_query": no_query,
+        "scheme": parsed.scheme.lower(),

+class SurfaceParser(HTMLParser):
+    def __init__(self, base_url: str) -> None:
+        super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True)
+        self.base_url = base_url
+        self.title_depth = 0
+        self.title_parts: list[str] = []
+        self.text_parts: list[str] = []
+        self.footer_depth = 0
+        self.footer_parts: list[str] = []
+        self.skip_depth = 0
+        self.anchors: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+        self.current_anchor: dict[str, Any] | None = None
+        self.forms: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+        self.current_form: dict[str, Any] | None = None
+        self.meta: dict[str, str] = {}
+        self.canonical_urls: list[str] = []
+        self.ldjson_depth = 0
+        self.ldjson_parts: list[str] = []
+        self.ldjson_blocks: list[str] = []
+
+    def handle_starttag(self, tag: str, attrs: list[tuple[str, str | None]]) -> None:
+        tag = tag.lower()
+        values = {key.lower(): value for key, value in attrs}
+        if tag == "title":
+            self.title_depth += 1
+        if tag in {"style", "noscript", "template"}:
+            self.skip_depth += 1
+        elif tag == "script":
+            script_type = normalize_space(values.get("type")).lower()
+            if script_type == "application/ld+json":
+                self.ldjson_depth += 1
+            else:
+                self.skip_depth += 1
+        elif tag == "footer":
+            self.footer_depth += 1
+        elif tag == "a":
+            href = values.get("href") or ""
+            if href:
+                self.current_anchor = {"href": href, "text_parts": [], "rel": normalize_space(values.get("rel")) or None}
+        elif tag == "form":
+            self.current_form = {
+                "form_index": len(self.forms) + 1,
+                "method": normalize_space(values.get("method") or "GET").upper(),
+                "action_raw": values.get("action") or self.base_url,
+                "id": normalize_space(values.get("id")) or None,
+                "name": normalize_space(values.get("name")) or None,
+                "controls": [],
+                "hidden_control_count": 0,
+            }
+            self.forms.append(self.current_form)
+        elif tag in {"input", "select", "textarea", "button"} and self.current_form is not None:
+            control_type = normalize_space(values.get("type") or tag).lower()
+            if control_type == "hidden":
+                self.current_form["hidden_control_count"] += 1
+            else:
+                self.current_form["controls"].append(
+                    {
+                        "tag": tag,
+                        "type": control_type,
+                        "name": normalize_space(values.get("name"))[:120] or None,
+                        "id": normalize_space(values.get("id"))[:120] or None,
+                        "required": "required" in values,
+                    }
+                )
+        elif tag == "meta":
+            key = normalize_space(values.get("name") or values.get("property")).lower()
+            content = normalize_space(values.get("content"))
+            if key in {"description", "og:title", "og:description", "og:site_name", "application-name"} and content:
+                sanitized = scrub_public_phrase(content, 300)
+                if sanitized:
+                    self.meta[key] = sanitized
+        elif tag == "link":
+            rel = normalize_space(values.get("rel")).lower()
+            href = values.get("href") or ""
+            if "canonical" in rel and href:
+                self.canonical_urls.append(href)
+
+    def handle_endtag(self, tag: str) -> None:
+        tag = tag.lower()
+        if tag == "title" and self.title_depth:
+            self.title_depth -= 1
+        if tag in {"style", "noscript", "template"} and self.skip_depth:
+            self.skip_depth -= 1
+        elif tag == "script":
+            if self.ldjson_depth:
+                self.ldjson_depth -= 1
+                block = "".join(self.ldjson_parts).strip()
+                if block:
+                    self.ldjson_blocks.append(block)
+                self.ldjson_parts = []
+            elif self.skip_depth:
+                self.skip_depth -= 1
+        elif tag == "footer" and self.footer_depth:
+            self.footer_depth -= 1
+        elif tag == "a" and self.current_anchor is not None:
+            anchor = dict(self.current_anchor)
+            anchor["text"] = scrub_public_phrase(" ".join(anchor.pop("text_parts")), 180)
+            self.anchors.append(anchor)
+            self.current_anchor = None
+        elif tag == "form":
+            self.current_form = None
+
+    def handle_data(self, data: str) -> None:
+        if self.ldjson_depth:
+            self.ldjson_parts.append(data)
+            return
+        if self.skip_depth:
+            return
+        if self.title_depth:
+            self.title_parts.append(data)
+        if self.current_anchor is not None:
+            self.current_anchor["text_parts"].append(data)
+        normalized = normalize_space(data)
+        if normalized:
+            self.text_parts.append(normalized)
+            if self.footer_depth:
+                self.footer_parts.append(normalized)
+
+    def result(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        return {
+            "title": scrub_public_phrase(" ".join(self.title_parts), 300),
+            "visible_text": normalize_space(" ".join(self.text_parts)),
+            "footer_text": normalize_space(" ".join(self.footer_parts)),
+            "anchors": self.anchors,
+            "forms": self.forms,
+            "meta": self.meta,
+            "canonical_urls": self.canonical_urls,
+            "ldjson_blocks": self.ldjson_blocks,
+        }

+def candidate_rows(route: dict[str, Any], text: str, footer_text: str, structured_rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    candidates: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+    seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
+
+    def add(candidate_class: str, value: Any, evidence_location: str) -> None:
+        sanitized = scrub_public_phrase(value, 260)
+        if not sanitized:
+            return
+        key = (candidate_class, sanitized.casefold())
+        if key in seen:
+            return
+        seen.add(key)
+        candidates.append(
+            {
+                "candidate_id": f"{route['route_id']}-candidate-{len(candidates) + 1:03d}",
+                "route_id": route["route_id"],
+                "receipt_id": route["receipt_id"],
+                "source_url": route["requested_url"],
+                "candidate_class": candidate_class,
+                "candidate_value": sanitized,
+                "evidence_location": evidence_location,
+                "identifier_grade": False,
+                "registry_grade": False,
+                "legal_entity_join_state": "candidate_only_unadjudicated",
+                "identity_admitted": False,
+                "negative_existence_claim_created": False,
+                "outside_human_dependency": False,
+                "graph_effect": "none",
+                "promotes_to": "candidate_only",
+            }
+        )
+
+    normalized_text = normalize_space(text)
+    for match in LEGAL_NAME_PATTERN.finditer(normalized_text):
+        add("explicit_schoolhouse_legal_name_candidate", match.group(0), "visible_text_pattern")
+    for match in SCHOOLHOUSE_LEGAL_CONTEXT_PATTERN.finditer(normalized_text):
+        add("schoolhouse_legal_status_phrase", match.group(0), "visible_text_pattern")
+    for match in COPYRIGHT_PATTERN.finditer(normalize_space(footer_text)):
+        add("footer_copyright_entity_phrase", match.group(0), "footer")
+    for row in structured_rows:
+        for field in ["legal_name", "name", "alternate_name", "parent_organization_name", "tax_id", "nonprofit_status"]:
+            if row.get(field):
+                candidate_class = "structured_data_tax_id_candidate" if field == "tax_id" else f"structured_data_{field}_candidate"
+                add(candidate_class, row[field], "json_ld")
+    return candidates

+        self.text_parts: list[str] = []

+        self.footer_parts: list[str] = []

+        if tag in {"style", "noscript", "template"}:
+            self.skip_depth += 1

+            self.footer_depth += 1

+            href = values.get("href") or ""
+            if href:
+                self.current_anchor = {"href": href, "text_parts": [], "rel": normalize_space(values.get("rel")) or None}

+            self.current_form = {
+                "form_index": len(self.forms) + 1,
+                "method": normalize_space(values.get("method") or "GET").upper(),
+                "action_raw": values.get("action") or self.base_url,
+                "id": normalize_space(values.get("id")) or None,

+        elif tag in {"input", "select", "textarea", "button"} and self.current_form is not None:

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Regenerate the sealed package to pass diff-check**

With the current sealed thirteen-file payload, this `git diff --cached --check` is the gate that exits with status 2, so the materializer stops before creating or pushing the permanent commit. Because the archive and per-file hashes are hard-coded earlier in the workflow, re-running cannot fix the failure; the payload needs to be regenerated so the staged additions are diff-clean, or this gate will keep blocking PR #1182 from receiving the files.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid mutating the product worktree before the allowlist**

When this workflow reaches the release gate, `npm run release:check` expands to `npm run check`, whose first step is `npm run compile`; those compile scripts rewrite timestamped build artifacts such as `build/axm-identity.json` and `build/migration-summary.json`. Because the changed-path allowlist is evaluated after this command, a successful release check leaves extra modified `build/*` files in the product worktree, so the `CHANGED` length/path tests reject the materialization before the push. Run the release gate in a separate clean worktree, or reset/generated-output changes before collecting `CHANGED`.

All 72 Archive metadata receipts now place the exact canonical CDX request in `locator_url` and preserve the original School.House subject page separately in `queried_url`. The builder asserts the reconstructed request against each committed `archive_query_url_sha256`; the permanent validator independently checks the receipt-to-attempt join, Archive host/path and full request, both query-hash fields, and the CDX response hash. No source was reacquired, no replay locator was dereferenced, and all prior denominators and authority states remain unchanged.

body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce the observed EIN verification**

When a downloaded XML member is wrong or the parser fails to observe the filer EIN, the runner still emits a terminal filing receipt with `filer_ein_verified: false`; this validation only checks that the declared `expected_ein` field is present. That would let a mismatched filing pass as one of the three terminal rows and corrupt the checksum artifact, so assert `filer_ein_verified == true` for successful receipt rows.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restore the truncated base64 bundle**

This bundle is not valid base64: every payload line is 76 characters except this 75-character line, leaving the total data length at 1 mod 4. In the `Validate replay custody` step, `base64 -d "$BUNDLE" | gzip -dc > "$RUNNER"` therefore exits nonzero under `set -o pipefail`, so the replay workflow fails before it can compile or execute the runner.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard scalar build fields before mapping**

When a schema-key-valid floor build has `controls` replaced by a scalar (for example corrupted JSON with `"controls": 0`), `validateCanonicalJsonTree` accepts the finite number and the top-level exact-key check still passes, so this line throws `TypeError: build.controls.map is not a function` instead of returning a refusal. That leaves the v48 validator/CLI unable to report exact scalar-type tampering as designed; validate that `controls` is an array before mapping it, and apply the same pattern to later array/object dereferences.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refresh legacy count assertions before running validator**

When this job reaches this validation step after a successful materialization, the decoded runner has already raised the manifest/source counts to 441 public-source rows and 27 coverage rows, but it only patches `tools/validate-bvvc-defense-capital.mjs` to import/call the new Form 990 validator; the existing archive-reconciliation block in that same top-level validator still hard-codes the previous 425/26 denominators. In the generated worktree this command therefore exits with archive reconciliation denominator drift before the product commit can be pushed, so the generated validator needs to update or derive those legacy assertions as part of the materialization.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Paid on exact clean product commit `a73690d05bcf83fa5110f8320df3d92e2dd94ffe`, tree `56c363fc980c506aa3913f4245fc43e03f3e348f`.

The repair guards every affected build container before array or nested-object dereference in both standalone PC-50 and compositional floor-v48 validation. It now rejects null/scalar top-level builds; scalar `controls`, requirement, source, custody, interpretation, frontier, and extension containers; and malformed nested control records through deterministic error returns rather than `TypeError` escape. The CLI validation paths inherit the same refusal behavior.

Regression coverage was added for scalar substitutions in both standalone and floor-v48 builds. The repair changed exactly four permanent files, preserved the same qualified parent, one-commit/fourteen-path topology, and zero transport paths.

Qualification:

```text
exact repair archive reconstruction       pass
four repaired file identities             pass
standalone PC-50 suite                     pass
complete floor-v48 ancestry                pass
no-magic-human                             pass
exact repaired-head workflow matrix    44 / 44 success
failed or pending workflows                  0
```

Repair custody: workflow `31051429125`, artifact `8951825267`, digest `sha256:adad7dc2a84b6d3b807363ac150a2aedf80d513b3c021b9a48f4e488db6577f4`.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject malformed fixtures before dereferencing them**

When the fixture JSON is `null`, this dereference throws `TypeError` after `requireExactKeys` has already recorded a validation error instead of returning deterministic refusal errors; null world entries and null sections similarly throw at later direct accesses. This affects both the standalone compiler and validator CLI and is distinct from the repaired build-container path, so guard the fixture and its nested containers before dereferencing them.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refuse a null v48 manifest before nested access**

When the v48 manifest file contains JSON `null`, canonical-tree validation permits the null leaf and `requireExactKeys` merely appends an error, after which this access throws `TypeError`. Consequently the floor compiler/validator cannot deterministically refuse this malformed source manifest; return a top-level object-type error before inspecting the nested manifest fields.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep ProPublica routes out of the official evidence class**

When consumers filter or weight receipts by provenance, this row incorrectly presents a request to `projects.propublica.org` as `evidence_class: "official"` and `source_type: "official_form_990_object_route_attempt"`; the repository’s existing source taxonomy identifies ProPublica as `primary_public` in `tools/build-graph.mjs:45`. The same misclassification appears on lines 6 and 9, inflates the manifest’s official-source count by three, and is locked in by the new validator’s requirement that every row be official, so these bridge attempts should retain third-party/primary-public provenance rather than IRS-official provenance.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate the new Florida-charity manifest counters**

When a regenerated or manually repaired package changes any of the newly added `schoolhouse_fl_charity_exact_query_*` manifest counters—for example, setting `schoolhouse_fl_charity_exact_query_guidance_success_rows` to a value that disagrees with the execution ledger—this validator still reports PASS. The block validates ledger aggregates and the two pre-existing global counts, but never compares the 18 new manifest counters with those aggregates, allowing downstream consumers of `manifest.json` to receive corrupted summary data; add these counters to `countChecks` or compare them directly with the execution, attempt, and custody records here.

When either fixed root or a selected candidate returns a redirect, the decoded `BoundedFetcher.fetch` calls `urllib.request.urlopen`, which follows the redirect before `final_url` is validated. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count rejected response reads against the aggregate cap**

When a response exceeds `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`, the decoded `BoundedFetcher.fetch` raises before adding the bytes already read to `aggregate_bytes`, so each failed download can consume 25,165,825 unreported bytes. Conversely, when an accepted read crosses the aggregate limit, the counter is left above the limit and the workflow's terminal `aggregate_response_bytes <= 100663296` assertion fails. Large report endpoints can therefore exceed the advertised network budget or fail terminal custody; enforce the remaining aggregate allowance while reading and count every byte consumed.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce the one-request bound across redirects**

If the fixed source responds with an HTTP redirect, the decoded runner's `urllib.request.urlopen()` follows it automatically before checking the final URL, so the transaction has already issued at least two GETs. The generated `source_requests` and request-bound fields remain hard-coded to one, and this assertion only validates those declarations; consequently, a same-host redirect whose final body has the expected hash can produce a successful artifact that falsely claims the one-request authority bound. Redirects should be disabled or explicitly counted and rejected before following them.

When the fixed source responds with a 301/302/307/308, the decoded runner's `fetch_source()` uses the default `urllib.request.urlopen` opener, which follows redirects automatically and can therefore issue multiple GETs before the final-URL and hash checks run. A same-host redirect to the expected body can even complete successfully while the artifact reports `source_requests: 1` and `maximum_total_requests: 1`, invalidating the workflow's request-bound custody; use a no-redirect handler or explicitly count and reject redirect responses.

body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail when either source has no anchor denominator**

When either GET has a transport error, non-200 response, disallowed redirect, or invalid content type, the reconstructed runner returns success with no observations for that route, and this branch explicitly accepts the empty ordinal list. Consequently, even a run where both sources fail passes validation and uploads an artifact with `current_anchor_rows == 0`, despite this step requiring a complete current denominator; require both receipts to be `accessible_html_anchor_denominator` before accepting the run.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The reconstructed runner uses curl's `--location` and checks `final_host` only after the redirected response has already been downloaded. The local curl manual says `--location` makes curl “redo the request on the new place,” so if either SOS route redirects to another HTTPS host, the workflow sends an out-of-scope GET before classifying it as disallowed, contradicting the asserted no-successor-fetch boundary; reject redirects or validate each `Location` host before following it.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce the byte limit during transfer**

This verifies only the byte count reported after acquisition, but the reconstructed runner invokes curl without a transfer-size limit, reads the complete body, and only then compares its length with `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`. A large or chunked provider response can therefore exceed both declared network bounds before the run fails; `curl --help all` exposes `--max-filesize <bytes>` as “Maximum file size to download,” or an equivalent streaming cap should be used.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Update the matrix current-result counters**

After this promotion, the matrix's authoritative `counts` and receipt report 228 terminal / 222 open cells and 118 terminal / 182 open substantive cells, but `current_result` still exposes the predecessor's 227/223 and 117/183 values. Any downstream consumer reading the matrix's result summary therefore sees the promotion as unreflected even though the North Dakota cell and aggregate counts changed; update these four values to the post-promotion totals and regenerate the matrix and dependent manifest hashes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate every manifest authority field**

When only `product-manifest.json` widens an authority claim, qualification still succeeds because the manifest is excluded from the full authority-boundary loop and this assertion checks only the two positive counters. I verified that `validateModel` accepts `manifest.authority_boundary.publication_effect = 'claimed'`; since the manifest is neither rebuilt nor self-hashed, the published schema's `none` constraint does not protect this eighth product in CI. Apply the same complete boundary validation to the manifest or actually validate it against the schema.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Paid in superseding clean one-parent PR #1771, exact head `07de734457c915af366ef3bcea3b15dd91f28576`.

The validator now routes `manifest.authority_boundary` through the same complete predicate used for input, decision, ledger, and summary. That predicate requires zero network and source authority, exact `1 / 1` field and matrix effects, zero row effects, open class, no cumulative-ledger effect, no publication, adoption, or graph effect, and no outside-human dependency.

The adversarial suite adds nine manifest-specific mutations, including the reproduced `publication_effect = 'claimed'` case. The validator, test, and self-describing manifest are the only changed product paths. The promoted matrix and all seven generated product documents remain byte-identical.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject undeclared manifest authority claims**

When the manifest contains every expected field plus an additional authority claim, this predicate checks only the known values and still qualifies it; for example, adding `prevalence_effect: "claimed"` to `manifest.authority_boundary` passes `validateModel`. Although the schema sets `additionalProperties: false`, the workflow never executes a JSON Schema validator, so the self-describing manifest can widen its authority boundary without any adversarial refusal. Validate the exact key set here or actually validate the documents against the published schema.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind manifest inventories to the declared paths**

When a malformed manifest leaves `hashed_file_count` at 13 but removes or duplicates an entry and recomputes `combined_sha256`, validation succeeds because this code only checks the scalar counts and then hashes whatever records remain. Likewise, the 14 `permanent_paths` values are never inspected, so they can be replaced with arbitrary unique strings. The workflow independently checks the Git diff, but it does not establish that the self-description lists that topology; compare both arrays against the exact expected path set and require the hashed entries to be unique and complete.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

body: Confirmed. This head is not admissible and will not be repaired or merged. Superseding PR #1771 carries the post-promotion matrix at SHA-256 `1878270c1c34d1a96b28eb0ee26eff5b1b3b6c8d74a56026c293544c7925d824`, whose `current_result` explicitly records `terminal_cells: "228/450"`, `still_open_cells: "222/450"`, `terminal_substantive_cells: 118`, and `still_open_substantive_cells: 182`. It also includes deterministic reconstruction, exact schema, focused validation, and thirty adversarial refusals, so the stale eight-path product is being retired rather than retained as a competing authority.

Paid in successor PR #1776 at repository-owner commit `ec9ec9f6cfc3180adcf816ae91e4bbf14df0e4dd`. The replacement validator requires the exact thirteen-key authority-boundary inventory for input, decision, ledger, summary, and manifest, and the adversarial suite now rejects `prevalence_effect: "claimed"` plus an undeclared manifest-root claim. PR #1771 is superseded and has no remaining merge authority.

Paid in successor PR #1776 at repository-owner commit `ec9ec9f6cfc3180adcf816ae91e4bbf14df0e4dd`. The manifest must now carry the exact ordered fourteen-path permanent inventory and exact ordered thirteen-path non-self hashed inventory, with unique complete paths and closed four-key file records. The new suite rejects omission, duplication, and path forgery even after `combined_sha256` is recomputed. PR #1771 is superseded and has no remaining merge authority.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fix the invalid assignment in the adversarial test**

When the new qualification workflow runs this test under Node 24, assigning to the value returned by `.at(-1)` raises `ReferenceError: Invalid left-hand side in assignment`. Execution therefore stops at this case before the adversarial suite can complete, so the workflow's "Rebuild and validate exact one-cell promotion" step always fails; assign through an array index or mutate a property instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Mutate the last permanent path through an array index**

When this adversarial case runs under the workflow's Node 24 setup, assigning to the result of `.at(-1)` raises `ReferenceError: Invalid left-hand side in assignment` before `reject` can call the validator. The repair workflow executes this test and then requires all 44 refusals at lines 90-91, so every qualification run stops here regardless of manifest correctness; assign through `permanent_paths[permanent_paths.length - 1]` instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

When a later PR changes another manifest-covered artifact—such as the promoted matrix, schema, builder, or milestone—the narrowed `pull_request.paths` and `push.paths` filters do not start this workflow. A repo-wide search shows that this is the only workflow invoking this specialized validator, and `release:check` does not include it, so such a change can leave the committed manifest checksums stale without the custody guard running. When a product commit weakens `required_final_matrix_rules` (for example, setting `all_preexisting_top_level_product_objects_must_remain_unchanged` to false) and regenerates the manifest hashes, this validator still succeeds because these rules and `required_refusals` are never asserted. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Align the schema with the current product parent**

For this exact-head product, the committed input custody and workflow bind parent `283c5993…`, but this closed schema still identifies historical validation merge `789c800d…` as the product parent. Consequently, any consumer validating the current contract against this schema rejects the valid current-parent value; the same stale identity is repeated in `$defs.inputCustody` (along with the old tree), while other constants still describe the prior promoted hash and manifest `@1`. The validator does not expose this because it inspects only the decision candidate constant, so update the schema's product identities to describe the committed current product while retaining `789c800d…` only as validation custody.

When the PR head is itself a merge commit whose first parent is `CANONICAL_PARENT`, this check still passes because, as documented by `gitrevisions(7)`, `<rev>^` is equivalent to `<rev>^1`; the later tree-diff checks likewise cannot detect the additional parent. Parse the product's `%P` list and require it to contain exactly the canonical parent.

When `main` advances by changing `MATRIX_PATH` (which is outside the seven product paths), the `pull_request` path still passes: the overlap check sees no product-path collision, this assertion checks the stale matrix in `PRODUCT_COMMIT`, and the validator also runs from that product commit. After merging, the `push` run instead reads the changed matrix from the merge tree and fails, so the required PR check can approve and admit a candidate against superseded input and detect it only after `main` has already changed; also require `BASE_SHA:$MATRIX_PATH` to equal `MATRIX_BLOB` (or validate the prospective merge tree).

In the `pull_request` path, `REPAIR_HEAD` is this commit (`bec911c`), whose sole parent is `REPAIR_PARENT` (`7d06800`), and this commit modifies both the workflow and manifest. Consequently `WORKFLOW_COMMIT` becomes `7d06800`, and this test compares that merge commit's parents (`5cbe9d8 a26be29`) with `7d06800`; it always fails under `set -e` before validation runs. Either split the repair into the two commits required by these assertions or validate the single commit's two-path diff directly.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Constrain the document fields in the published schema**

The schema requires these ledger fields but assigns each an empty schema, so Draft 2020-12 validation accepts values such as `"row_state_mutation_count": "corrupt"` and `"transition": null`. The promoted matrix, census, summary, and index definitions below have the same issue. Although the repository-specific JavaScript validator catches the current files through deterministic hashes, consumers using this published schema—and the workflow step claiming to validate all eight documents—receive no type or value validation for most of the product.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The unindented `\'\'\'` terminates the `run: |` block scalar, and the following text is interpreted as top-level YAML; parsing the committed workflow fails at this line with `could not find expected ':'`. GitHub therefore cannot register or run this temporary materialization workflow for any pull request. All embedded heredoc content in this `run` block must retain the block's YAML indentation.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not treat a rejected push as object transfer**

When GitHub rejects this push because the token cannot update workflow files, this branch records `object_transferred_ref_refused`, sets `EXIT_CODE` to zero, and completes even though it has just verified that the target ref does not exist. A rejected receive-pack does not preserve the uploaded commit: Git places incoming objects in quarantine and removes them when the pre-receive operation fails, as documented in [git-receive-pack’s quarantine behavior](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-receive-pack#_quarantine_environment). Thus the expected permission-rejection path can produce a green run without materializing either the commit object or `TARGET_BRANCH`; use credentials permitted to publish the workflow-bearing commit or fail this path instead.

Capture the push payload's `before` SHA and require it to equal `P1` so the merge is bound to the canonical main tip that existed before this push.

body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare product tree-entry modes as well as blob IDs**

For a crafted canonical merge, these checks permit an alternate HEAD tree in which any added product path has the product blob but a different tree-entry mode, such as `100755` instead of `100644`. `git rev-parse commit:path` returns only the referenced object ID, while `git diff -h` defines `--name-only` as showing only changed file names, so the surrounding addition-only denominator does not establish mode equality either. Compare the full `git ls-tree` entries for all fourteen paths (or otherwise bind the resulting tree) before claiming the exact product tree was admitted.

body:
Resolved through a canonical external admission control rather than by making this product self-referential. PR #1910 merged as `966ea44274ff0372d3b0fa8e25e18d4e98f0b7cb` and supplies an immutable anchor for exact product commit `30e4f3c17848419790d27826199e37df942c351f`, exact tree `f1a05ffc235228a852387104f1175a882cae0e49`, sole construction parent `0840358962621b0be3db6864ecec763327f35903`, message bytes, fourteen-path denominator, entry modes, and product-blob identities. Its read-only workflow takes those identities from the canonical PR base, requires the event head itself to equal the pinned commit and tree, reconstructs and rehashes the raw commit object, checks the full path/status/mode/blob denominator, and independently replays the product.

The refreshed exact-head matrix against base `966ea442…` is green: external anchor run `31466467308`, dedicated product run `31466467234`, Release `31466467306`, No magic human `31466467321`, compact `31466467284`, and Wave 01 `31466467244`. The product head and all fourteen product bytes remain unchanged. The mechanism therefore rejects the executable-mode and manifest-reordering counterexamples identified here without embedding a circular self-SHA or self-tree in the product. The control question is whether any alternate product commit or tree can now pass the canonical external anchor while the event head remains `30e4f3c1…`; the current controls require exact equality before semantic replay.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject prototype-rewritten Web API exotic brands**

When a caller replaces a fixture record with a `URL`, `URLSearchParams`, `Headers`, or `FormData`, resets its prototype to `Object.prototype`, and copies the expected enumerable fields onto it, none of these predicates detects the retained internal brand. `validateFixture` consequently accepts the exotic with the exact expected snapshot hash because `stableJson` ignores its hidden slots, defeating the validator's fail-closed canonical-JSON and prototype-rewritten-exotic custody guarantee. Extend brand detection to cover these Web API objects or otherwise reject objects retaining non-JSON internal slots.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-extensible disguised Web API objects**

When a prototype-rewritten `Headers` or `FormData` is made non-extensible after the expected world fields are copied onto it, its direct intrinsic `has` probe throws under Node 24 and this condition skips the temporary native-prototype probe. Fresh evidence in this revision is that `validateFixture` returns `[]` for both objects after `Object.setPrototypeOf(value, Object.prototype)`, `Object.assign(...)`, and `Object.preventExtensions(value)`, so the exotic-brand bypass remains available despite the new guard.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Return validation errors for malformed world shapes**

When syntactically valid fixture JSON contains `null` or another non-object as a world, canonical validation accepts that JSON value and `exactKeys` records an error, but execution continues here and dereferences it. For example, replacing `worlds[0]` with `null` makes `validateFixture` throw `TypeError` instead of returning its error ledger, causing the validator API and CLI to crash on malformed input rather than reporting the rejected fixture.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
