**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Commit every regenerated public artifact**

After the preceding release check regenerates outputs for the added surface and receipt, this explicit staging list omits materially changed tracked artifacts, including `build/cases/uk-ai-policy.json`, `build/report-frontier.json`, `build/scout-report.md`, and `reports/index.html`. For example, the regenerated case contains the new terms receipt and reports 16 receipts, while the version left in the pushed commit still exposes the old 15-receipt data. Stage the affected case/report/public artifacts as well so the committed generated release agrees with the newly staged ledgers and catalog.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep Tech.eu-only investors off the February 11 slice**

For the investors supported only by Tech.eu (this row and the similar Cal Henderson, Tom Shinner, and Louis Mosley rows), the sole receipt was published on February 12 and its checked-in extract does not identify a February 11 transaction or participation event; February 11 is the separate company announcement, which did not name these investors. Assigning a one-day February 11 window therefore makes time-sliced queries emit paths such as Andreessen–Salama on February 11 while rejecting February 12, inventing day-level precision without receipt support. Leave these windows undated or model the February 12 report as a separate bounded surface unless an exact event date is sourced.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude duplicate tenure observations from recurrence scoring**

When scores are regenerated, this tenure surface is counted in addition to the incorporation surface even though both describe the same directorship and use the same receipt. `scoreActor` counts every participation surface toward density, type recurrence, and `machine_raw` without deduplicating the underlying relationship, so Alex Cooper now acquires a `model_governance_surface` recurrence score of 2, Ben Warner gains another surface, and the resulting normalization changes scores for every entity. Keep these observation-only tenure records out of scoring or deduplicate them from the incorporation record before calculating recurrence.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Regenerate the committed graph artifacts**

This patch changes the canonical surfaces, participations, receipts, and claims without committing the corresponding generated files. A fresh checkout served with `npm run serve` loads the tracked `build/surface-graph.json` and `build/receipt-graph.json` directly from `app.js`, so neither new surface nor any of the seven receipts and six claims appears in the UI; running `npm run compile` produces substantial tracked changes across those graphs, scores, and identity artifacts. Commit the regenerated outputs so static consumers receive the data introduced here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the two role observations as separate windows**

For dates between the two source events (for example, 2020-07-01), this row is exported as a dated `participates_in` claim valid continuously from 2020-03-13 through 2021-05-13. The receipts only establish Warner's role during the March 13–16 record and again on May 13, while the row's own note explicitly disclaims continuous tenure. Represent these as separate observation windows/rows (or omit the unsupported interval) so temporal consumers do not infer participation throughout the intervening fourteen months.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prove the ASI-to-Faculty entity join before admitting hops**

When the all-time Ben Warner → Matt Clifford route is queried, this surface treats the Zebra profile's “ASI Data Science” and Companies House's “Advanced Skills Initiative Limited” (company 08873131) as the same legal entity, but neither of the two cited receipt extracts establishes that brand-to-company identity; the pre-existing canonical alias is not source evidence for this new hop. Consequently the Ben/Marc/Saul co-participation edges—and therefore the advertised two-hop route through a Faculty director—are not supported by the receipts attached here. Add a receipt that explicitly resolves ASI Data Science to company 08873131, or keep this surface non-hop until that join is established.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add ASI/Faculty to the service surface**

When this ledger is compiled, participation rows are the only structured source for surface participants, AXM claims, and organization scores. After removing the Warner rows, this new row leaves Vote Leave as the sole organization, even though the receipt's only positive proposition is that ASI Data Science worked for Vote Leave and the canonical `faculty` organization represents ASI Data Science. Consequently the provider side disappears from the compiled relationship and Faculty does not inherit this scorable campaign surface; add a source-supported `faculty` organization participation row rather than encoding the relationship only in prose.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid publishing an unsupported full-year window**

The replacement receipt and extract establish only that ASI Data Science worked for Vote Leave; they provide no service start or end date, while their recorded event date is the 2018 testimony. In this repository, `time_start: "2016"` and `time_end: "2016"` are expanded by `tools/lib/temporal.mjs` to 2016-01-01 through 2016-12-31 and published in the surface and AXM claims, so the newly “official” record asserts a full-year validity interval that the surviving evidence does not support. Leave the relationship undated or bind it to dates established by a receipt.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep the BARS application distinct from an appointment**

The new receipt extract states only that the Commission considered Case's application for the role; it does not establish that he accepted or began the appointment, and 11 June is identified as the page's publication date rather than a role start date. Because this surface removes the Times receipt and relies exclusively on that application record, encoding Case as an actual participant in an “appointment” on 11 June causes downstream scoring and governance-continuity outputs to treat an unconfirmed role as fact. Retain corroborating evidence of uptake or model this as a Business Appointment Rules application/advice observation instead.

Addressed in commit `34a2f0b9e6f54a3084194a480847e722c61e8a0f`. The receipt remains a bounded `repository_content` record for the Commerce-to-Intel performance-linked equity mechanism, and it now distinguishes the period flow from the cumulative operated state. The claim, Q2 2026 locator, and instrument-quantity ledger record approximately 3 million escrowed shares released by fiscal year-end 2025, approximately 13 million released during the six months ended 27 June 2026, approximately 16 million released cumulatively by that date, and approximately 143 million remaining in escrow.

The validator freezes those quantities and enforces `3,000,000 + 13,000,000 = 16,000,000`; the boundary `period_release_is_cumulative_release` remains false; and a mutation that substitutes 13 million for the cumulative field fails closed. This correction widens the map without overstating realization: Intel operated the escrow release, Commerce retained the public securities interest, and the bounded record still shows no sale, dividend, warrant exercise, federal cash receipt, public-account booking, or affected-party distribution. The controlling question is whether a period release can be represented as the cumulative operated state; the repaired receipt and arithmetic control now require the answer to be no.

Addressed in commit `34a2f0b9e6f54a3084194a480847e722c61e8a0f`. The resale-registration source is now treated as a quantitatively bounded registration record, not merely a categorical securities reference. Its frozen locator identifies potential resale by the United States Department of Commerce of a warrant covering up to 240,516,150 shares and 673,839,150 common shares, and it decomposes the common-share registration into 274,583,000 delivered shares, 158,740,000 escrowed shares, and 240,516,150 shares issuable upon warrant exercise.

The instrument-quantity ledger and validator enforce `274,583,000 + 158,740,000 + 240,516,150 = 673,839,150`, compare the exact locator and quantity object, and reject both quantity drift and incomplete registration language. The wider control remains intact: Commerce is the registered selling securityholder, Intel is the issuer, registration makes a sale legally available, and the receipt still refuses to infer that a sale, warrant exercise, federal cash realization, or public distribution occurred. The controlling question is whether a registration account can validate without the exact registered quantities and component arithmetic; the repaired object now makes that omission fail closed.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pin the substantive source records**

The source checks validate only shape and host boundaries rather than the frozen values: replacing any locator with unrelated strings of at least 25 characters still passes, as do changing an authority, using any syntactically valid publication date, or substituting another URL on an allowed host. This lets the nine source IDs remain unchanged while the evidence supporting the authorized claim is materially rewritten under a green validator; compare each source's authority, record type, date, URL, and locator array against an exact expected record.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate all declared dependency binding metadata**

For each predecessor binding, only `path` and `blob_sha` are checked. Removing or changing the candidate's declared `schema_version`, `pull_request`, or `merge_commit` therefore produces no validation error—for example, the Intel binding can claim an unrelated PR and merge while its blob check remains green. Because these fields are part of the frozen provenance record, include them in the exact binding expectations rather than silently accepting binding-metadata drift.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require the complete expected-state field set**

Iterating over the candidate-controlled `expected_state` keys makes removal fail open: deleting `hfu_repository_promotion_allowed`, `cross_domain_regression_completed`, and `issue_345_may_close` still returns no errors because those invariants are never visited. Require the exact expected key set before comparing values so an omitted safety field cannot disappear from the frozen ledger while validation succeeds.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed in `ff83ac3769b5223ab039ca0e5d6cfd9e31f6966e`, preserved unchanged at current head `72a0c155523dbbb705d5c2a1a55c9643075fa97d`. The frozen candidate is now guarded twice: the library compares the canonicalized complete object against `HFU_SHARE_CANDIDATE_JSON_SHA256`, while the executable validator checks the raw file against both its Git blob SHA and SHA-256 before semantic validation. This closes authority, record-type, date, URL, locator, ordering, and undeclared-field drift, including the same-host and locator mutations added to the adversarial suite.

The exact complete-object digest causes deletion, substitution, addition, or reordering of any `expected_state` field to fail before candidate-controlled iteration can omit it. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require the complete guarded-nonfinding set**

When a guarded nonfinding is deleted from an adjudication, this validation still passes because it requires only one remaining key and then checks only the supplied entries. For example, removing `identified_federal_cash_receipt` from the Intel decision succeeds while the resulting reconciliation no longer preserves that explicit guard, contrary to the frozen nonfinding ledger; compare the guarded keys against the complete per-candidate `nonfindings` set rather than accepting any nonempty subset.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject missing route guardrails**

When a later edit removes `route_guardrails` entirely or deletes an individual guardrail, `Object.entries(row.route_guardrails||{})` simply iterates over no entry for the missing boundary, so the validator still succeeds; I confirmed that deleting the first frontier's entire guardrail object exits successfully. This allows the frozen artifact to lose explicit safety constraints while its validation gate remains green, so validate the required guardrail keys or exact expected objects before checking that their values are false.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The reconciliation JSON and every empirical receipt remain byte-identical, so the evidence-only authority contract stays `authorized_answer_scope: none` and the existing expected ledger remains five claim-evidence records, zero effective answers, false completion, and `issue_345_may_close: false`.

The current head updates the live library, fail-closed validator, adversarial test, workflow dependency filters, and downstream frontier atomically. The validator now binds and evaluates the Robodebt receipt, compares the pre-implementation and final contracts, permits only the authorized false-to-true `pre_action_timing` transition, and requires every other answer field and domain record to remain unchanged. body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require the hash domain to match the capture mode**

For decoded HTTP responses, the contract permits `body_capture_mode`, `body_hash_domain`, and the two predecessor digest-domain fields to disagree: it only requires the origin and custody domains to match each other. A record can therefore declare a post-decoding capture while assigning `body_hash_domain` to pre-decoding payload octets and still satisfy every rule, leaving the exact hashed bytes ambiguous. Add an explicit equality or allowed-crosswalk invariant tying the capture mode, general hash domain, and both predecessor digest domains together.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind every redirect hop to retrievable authentication evidence**

For a request that follows redirects, each intermediate hop can satisfy this manifest with only a `connection_authentication_receipt_id`; unlike the stage-level receipt, the hop has no required digest or custody locator. An unavailable or substituted receipt therefore leaves the hop structurally valid even though the amendment promises independently authenticated, retrievable evidence for every redirect peer. Require each hop to carry the connection-authentication receipt hash and custody locator, or another enforceable binding to the exact receipt.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Define the source-native authentication receipt alternative**

When a source uses the explicitly allowed `source_native_transport` or `source_native_session`, this rule says a source-native peer-authentication receipt may replace the TLS transcript, but the contract defines no fields for that receipt: every stage still requires a TLS-peer receipt, and the TLS receipt schema unconditionally requires SNI, ALPN, certificates, and TLS transcript fields. Such a source cannot satisfy the declared alternative without fabricating TLS data or placing native evidence into unrelated TLS fields. Add a concrete source-native receipt hash/custody schema and make the TLS requirements conditional on the transport.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Limit wrapper ownership to the current narrative context**

When any earlier text contains an unmatched opener—even in a previous sentence or paragraph—this new condition enables wrapper preservation for the later phone because `availableOuterOpeners` was calculated over the entire input prefix. For example, `Broken ( paragraph\n\nPhone: +81 3 6216 5111)` now becomes `Broken ( paragraph\n\nPhone: [contact omitted])`, retaining an ownerless closer that the prior behavior discarded. Bound the opener search to the phone's current narrative context rather than treating every unmatched opener in the document as its wrapper.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject acquisition URLs outside the resolved authority**

When an authority receipt lists an official host such as `www.sec.gov` but the origin and acquisition receipts use another HTTPS host, the graph still validates because these URLs are checked only for HTTPS syntax and are never reconciled with `official_origin_hosts` or with each other. A custody-complete receipt can therefore attribute an attacker-controlled document to an official authority; compare the requested, resolved, redirect, origin, and evidence URLs against the authority resolution before accepting it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve symlinked ancestors before accepting receipt files**

When any directory below `receipts/m05/intel-realization/` is a symlink, `lstatSync(target)` resolves that intermediate symlink and reports the final external target as a regular file. Thus a lexically in-prefix binding can read and approve files elsewhere in the repository or filesystem, despite the contract prohibiting path escape and symlinked receipt objects; validate every path component or compare the real path against the real controlled root.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Derive credential status from the captured request headers**

When the retrievable request-header object contains an `Authorization`, `Cookie`, or similar credential but the acquisition JSON declares `request_contains_credentials: false`, validation succeeds because it trusts that boolean and treats the header bytes as opaque. This defeats the contract's public, credential-free request boundary and can approve or commit sensitive authenticated acquisition material; inspect the captured headers rather than relying solely on the declaration.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

When two uncertainty intervals overlap, the contract explicitly leaves their ordering indeterminate, but each stage only rejects a definite contradiction and merely requires the `temporal_order_reconciliation` field to exist. Unlike freshness, there is no `temporal_reconciliation_result_must_be_pass` requirement, so a populated but indeterminate reconciliation can satisfy the declared stage contract even though `expected_result` claims all four stages require interval-safe chronology.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed at exact live-main child `9ccd3f086a86eb77e30a483ef0d4c3ab060cd531`. This was a local-label isolation defect in the narrative-period classifier: the prior suffix-only match let ordinary prose ending in `contact`, `phone`, `fax`, or `mobile` act as telephone-label punctuation. `isNarrativePeriodAbbreviation(...)` now extracts the candidate label and inspects the complete local construct before it. The period is exempted only when the label is isolated at the current context start, after a structural line boundary, or after an explicit wrapper or field delimiter. Intervening prose therefore leaves the period as a sentence boundary, while exact forms such as `Tel.`, `Phone.`, `Phone No.`, and line-isolated labels remain in context.

The regression block covers all four reported prose suffixes in ASCII and fullwidth forms, the positive exact-label set, and a structural line-boundary control. Hosted First-party industrial-exhaust intake #256, No magic human gate #3696, and Release checks #6283 are attached to this unchanged SHA and remain pending runner assignment.

The control question is whether any ordinary prose prefix can still make one of these suffix words the whole local label construct, or any structurally isolated telephone label can now be severed from its legitimate wrapper context.

The classifier now extracts one trailing lexical or dotted token, calls `isDomainLikeNarrativeToken(...)` first, and refuses abbreviation treatment for domain-shaped tokens with valid dotted labels and a terminal alphabetic label. Only after that rejection does `isMultiPeriodNarrativeAbbreviation(...)` admit repeated-letter initialisms or the bounded doctoral forms.

Phone: ...` fails similarly through the single-period allowlist. The exemption needs surrounding context that distinguishes an abbreviation continuing the current sentence from one ending it.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Load the previous receipt for scheduled comparisons**

Every scheduled or push run starts from a clean checkout and invokes the runner without `--previous`, while no earlier artifact is downloaded or otherwise restored. Consequently `previousReceipt` is always null in this workflow, every observation gets `changed_since_previous: null`, and `changed_routes` remains zero even when an official route's representation changes between runs. Persist and load the last validated receipt before executing the recurring watch.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate receipt status fields as a coherent state**

For externally supplied or reconstructed receipts, this one-way check does not bind `status`, `metadata_only`, `content_success`, `route_success`, `body_bytes`, and `body_sha256` together. For example, a row with `status: "metadata_only"`, `metadata_only: false`, and `content_success: true` passes after recalculating the self-hash, causing the derived summary to count the same route as both metadata-only and a content success; similarly, `content_retrieved` can carry zero bytes and no digest. Enforce the complete invariants for each terminal status so the validator cannot certify internally contradictory observations.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat an unspaced slash as an identifier boundary**

The hard-boundary predicate requires whitespace on at least one side of `/`, although `PHONE_SPAN_PATTERN` accepts a bare slash inside one candidate. Fresh evidence on this exact head is `ID: 12345678/03-6216-8041` (and its fullwidth-slash equivalent), which remains entirely unchanged: the unscored identifier is preserved correctly, but the independently complete phone after the slash is exposed. Recognize the unspaced slash boundary before recursively classifying the suffix.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retain URL provenance before a detached wrapper**

When a long URL path ends in `/reference:` and the following international phone is wrapped, `currentTokenWithTrailingSpace` captures only the detached `(`, so this function falls back to the last 64 characters and discards the distant URL host. Fresh evidence on this exact head is ``https://example.test/${'a'.repeat(140)}/reference: (+81 3 6216 5111)``, which remains completely unchanged; the bounded label matcher therefore regains identifier authority and exposes the independent phone after whitespace. The retained context must include the complete preceding URL token even when an opening wrapper follows that whitespace.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require verified index bodies to match the path digest**

When a retained byte-verified index receipt is modified, its `body` and `body_sha256` can be changed together without renaming the content-addressed file, and this validator still accepts it because `computedBodySha256` is never compared with `receipt.index_sha256` or `pathIndexSha256`. `writeIndexReceipt` establishes all three digests from the same HTML, so this omission lets `validateIndustrialExhaustReceiptStore`—and runtime custody when an unchanged referenced anchor remains—admit altered index bytes as verified.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

This thread identifies the unscored identifier-prefix recursion defect. Final owner-authored commit `1b1ad30dbf44eb145b74de09252760aa8115dfb5` routes explicit identifier context through `identifierProtectedPrefixEnd`. When no protected prefix slice independently scores as a phone, that function scans the separators between digit groups, recognizes hard boundaries, verifies that the suffix can start an independent phone, and returns the suffix offset so `phoneRedactionRanges` recurses with corrected coordinates. The focused suite now fixes the reported case at `ID: 12345678 / 03-6216-8041` and also covers period, international, semicolon, and explicit phone-label variants. The exact tree `ae67e9bd5ed125d2fc631e7030b596921e0beb49` passed materializer run `32594551050` and fresh exact-head runs `32594656950`, `32594656864`, and `32594656915`. The control question is whether any unscored identifier prefix can still carry protection across a separator that begins an independently valid telephone value.

This thread identifies loss of URL provenance when the identifier-label match is found inside a bounded suffix. On final commit `1b1ad30dbf44eb145b74de09252760aa8115dfb5`, `explicitIdentifierLabelMatch` still bounds the label search to the final 128 characters, but converts the match position back to an absolute offset and passes the complete retained normalized prefix preceding that offset to `hasUrlTokenPrefixContext`. The URL predicate therefore retains the scheme or host even when it is more than 128 characters behind `/id:` or `/reference:`. The regression matrix covers long HTTP, protocol-relative, bare-domain, and IP-host tokens, and requires the URL text to survive while the telephone value after whitespace redacts. Tree `ae67e9bd5ed125d2fc631e7030b596921e0beb49` passed materializer run `32594551050` and exact-head runs `32594656950`, `32594656864`, and `32594656915`. The control question is whether any retained URL token can still lose its introducer before identifier-label rejection evaluates the absolute match position.

This exact-head finding is closed by the same full-token custody mechanism now present in commit `1b1ad30dbf44eb145b74de09252760aa8115dfb5`. The bounded matcher determines only where the terminal identifier label begins; it then reconstructs that position in the complete normalized prefix and tests all preceding text with `hasUrlTokenPrefixContext`, rather than testing the truncated 128-character window. Long HTTP, scheme-relative, bare-domain, and IP-host cases are executable regressions in `test/industrial-exhaust.test.js`. The final library blob is `5434f1cd0403e3a82febfc3684f8333b43f6f0d0`, the test blob is `48f89f0a058a0d0395cb45cf16c088c9a3812b9c`, and the materializer plus all three final-head workflows passed. The control question is whether any bounded label-search operation still changes the provenance text supplied to the URL classifier.

This thread identifies the unspaced slash-boundary defect. Final commit `1b1ad30dbf44eb145b74de09252760aa8115dfb5` changes the fallback boundary predicate in `identifierProtectedPrefixEnd` to recognize `/` and `／` anywhere in the separator, without requiring whitespace. It then calls `canStartIndependentPhone` before recursing, which preserves `ID: 12345678/87654321` while rendering `ID: 12345678/03-6216-8041` as `ID: 12345678/[contact omitted]`; the fullwidth equivalent is also pinned. The exact two-file tree passed materializer run `32594551050`, the complete release gate, and all three fresh PR workflows. The control question is whether any slash glyph accepted by `PHONE_SPAN_PATTERN` can still join a protected identifier to an independently valid telephone suffix without triggering recursive classification.

This thread identifies URL-provenance loss when the scanner candidate is preceded by a detached opening wrapper. In final commit `1b1ad30dbf44eb145b74de09252760aa8115dfb5`, `redactionPrefixContext` recognizes wrapper-only tokens such as `(` and `（`, walks backward to the preceding non-whitespace token, and expands `contextStart` to retain that complete token. `explicitIdentifierLabelMatch` can therefore see that `/reference:` or `/id:` belongs to a long URL and rejects its narrative-label authority before the wrapped international telephone value is classified. The focused suite pins both a long absolute URL followed by `(+81 3 6216 5111)` and a long protocol-relative URL followed by `（＋８１ ３ ６２１６ ５１１１）`; both preserve the URL and wrapper while redacting only the phone. Tree `ae67e9bd5ed125d2fc631e7030b596921e0beb49` passed materializer run `32594551050` and fresh exact-head runs `32594656950`, `32594656864`, and `32594656915`. The control question is whether any supported detached opening wrapper can still sever a retained URL token from the label classifier that governs the following candidate.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Check boundaries before accepting a scored identifier prefix**

When a later independent phone begins with a parenthesized area code, the prefix search can score a slice that includes that area code more highly than the identifier alone, and this early return prevents the suffix boundary logic below from running. Fresh evidence on this exact head is `ID: 09012345678 / (03) 6216 8041`, which remains entirely unchanged; the same failure occurs with fullwidth parentheses and with the grouped identifier `ID: 01 42 68 53 00 / (03) 6216 8041`. The protected-prefix selection must not consume the opening group of a separately valid phone before recursively classifying its suffix.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recognize whitespace after an unscored identifier**

When an unscored identifier and a complete domestic phone share a scanner candidate with only whitespace between them, this predicate finds no boundary and leaves the phone exposed. Fresh evidence on this exact head is `ID: 12345678 03-6216-8041`, which is returned unchanged, even though the focused matrix already treats the same whitespace as an independent-phone boundary after scored identifiers. The fallback needs to recognize a whitespace-separated suffix when `canStartIndependentPhone` confirms that the suffix is independently complete.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Classify challenge bodies before requiring a 2xx response**

When a recognized Cloudflare, Incapsula, or Akamai challenge is returned with its common 403 or 503 status, the `response.ok` guard prevents `isChallengePage` from running, so the route is recorded as a generic `http_failure` rather than `challenge_page`. This makes the challenge-page count inaccurate and can cause challenge-generated body changes to be reported as ordinary route changes; inspect eligible HTML error responses for challenge markers before selecting the terminal status.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

This P1 is closed on final owner-authored commit `8cb8d44c50a6fd2ba1da1121e251155867bc01bf`. `identifierProtectedPrefixEnd` no longer accepts arbitrary scored slices before considering later-phone boundaries. It first preserves the entire candidate only when the complete pre-observation span independently scores as one phone-shaped identifier. Otherwise it enumerates separators whose suffix independently passes `canStartIndependentPhone`, scores only the prefix ending before that validated suffix, and prefers the longest complete scored prefix. A later phone’s opening `(03)` therefore cannot extend identifier scope merely because the combined prefix receives a parenthesized score; the boundary remains before the opening wrapper. The focused suite now pins `ID: 09012345678 / (03) 6216 8041`, its fullwidth equivalent, `ID: 01 42 68 53 00 / (03) 6216 8041`, and whitespace-only parenthesized variants, while guard cases preserve complete North American and ambiguous numeric identifiers. Tree `f467ec30d26b31b14d10e2149f802b9e99e59651` passed materializer run `32607470719` and fresh exact-head runs `32607600247`, `32607600259`, and `32607600262`. The control question is whether any suffix can still be absorbed into protected scope without itself leaving an independently complete telephone candidate at the proposed boundary.

This P1 is closed on final owner-authored commit `8cb8d44c50a6fd2ba1da1121e251155867bc01bf`. The boundary enumerator now recognizes normalized whitespace as a candidate separator, but it still requires `canStartIndependentPhone` to prove that the suffix is independently complete. For an unscored prefix, a whitespace-only split is admitted only at the first numeric boundary and only after at least seven protected digits; stronger slash and sentence-period boundaries retain their existing route. The exact regression `ID: 12345678 03-6216-8041` now renders as `ID: 12345678 [contact omitted]`, and the suite also covers a parenthesized suffix. Counter-controls preserve `ID: 1 212 555 1234`, `ID: 999 212 555 1234`, and `ID: 12345678 87654321`, preventing whitespace from becoming an unconditional split. Tree `f467ec30d26b31b14d10e2149f802b9e99e59651` passed materializer run `32607470719`, release run `32607600247`, no-magic run `32607600259`, and intake run `32607600262`, whose crawl job was skipped. The control question is whether any whitespace-only split can proceed without both a bounded identifier prefix and an independently valid telephone suffix.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Split after grouped unscored identifiers**

When an unscored identifier itself contains multiple numeric groups, the `first === 1` restriction prevents a plain-whitespace split even when the prefix is explicitly labelled, has at least seven digits, and the suffix is independently telephone-valid. For example, `ID: 1234 5678 03-6216-8041` is returned unchanged, whereas the previous implementation redacted the final phone; the same leak occurs with `ID: 123-45678 090-1234-5678`. The boundary validation should use the bounded prefix and independently valid suffix rather than requiring the identifier to occupy exactly one digit group.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept nested identifier wrappers**

The optional wrapper portion accepts only one opening character, so explicitly labelled identifiers wrapped by more than one accepted delimiter lose protection. For example, `ID: [(+81 3 6216 5111)]` becomes `ID: [([contact omitted])]`, and `ＩＤ：（（＋８１ ３ ６２１６ ５１１１））` is likewise corrupted, even though the surrounding context logic already walks multiple wrapper-only tokens. Allowing a sequence of accepted opening wrappers would preserve these phone-shaped identifiers.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

This P1 is closed on final owner-authored commit `2985317cda6599c4869d35a84b66d074d9a178a7`. `identifierProtectedPrefixEnd` still requires `canStartIndependentPhone` to establish an independently complete suffix and still requires at least seven digits in an unscored protected prefix, but it no longer requires that prefix to occupy exactly one digit group. Grouped and hyphenated identifiers can therefore end at a later validated whitespace boundary. The focused suite now pins `ID: 1234 5678 03-6216-8041`, `ID: 123-45678 090-1234-5678`, the fullwidth grouped form, and a parenthesized suffix. Existing counter-controls continue to preserve `ID: 1 212 555 1234`, `ID: 999 212 555 1234`, and `ID: 12345678 87654321`, because no proposed split satisfies both the bounded-prefix digit floor and an independently valid telephone suffix. Tree `cdb3c2c213efe6e5d26926fd5d51b4c4ac46589d`, library blob `ac809bab014f951f4736030d130358439052eb92`, and test blob `322fe508467a2e45ddbb67684e87976166203446` passed materializer run `32608152421` and fresh exact-head runs `32608257286`, `32608257297`, and `32608257312`; the crawl job was skipped. The control question is whether any grouped unscored prefix can now be split without both seven protected digits and an independently complete telephone suffix.

This P2 is closed on final owner-authored commit `2985317cda6599c4869d35a84b66d074d9a178a7`. The terminal wrapper clause in `EXPLICIT_IDENTIFIER_LABEL_PATTERN` now accepts a sequence of the already approved ASCII and fullwidth opening delimiters, with optional whitespace after each delimiter, rather than exactly one delimiter. The focused suite preserves `ID: [(+81 3 6216 5111)]`, `ID: [ (+81 3 6216 5111)]`, and `ＩＤ：（（＋８１ ３ ６２１６ ５１１１））`. Counter-regressions require a phone-labelled nested value to redact and require a nested wrapped phone after an arbitrarily long URL-embedded `/id:` token to redact without losing the URL prefix, so wrapper generalization cannot override phone-label precedence or URL provenance. Tree `cdb3c2c213efe6e5d26926fd5d51b4c4ac46589d`, library blob `ac809bab014f951f4736030d130358439052eb92`, and test blob `322fe508467a2e45ddbb67684e87976166203446` passed materializer run `32608152421`, artifact receipt `9484726365` with digest `sha256:3e46be9e8b6336b1749685e72bc5eacf4b192e29e464be7195b2921baf4d184a`, and fresh exact-head runs `32608257286`, `32608257297`, and `32608257312`. The control question is whether any accepted opening-wrapper sequence can still sever an explicit identifier label, suppress an affirmative phone label, or erase retained URL provenance.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Split before scoring the later parenthesized phone**

When a short identifier and a later local phone total at most 15 digits, the later phone's opening parenthesis makes the entire combined span score as one candidate, so this early return bypasses every validated boundary. For example, `ID: 1234567 / (123) 4567` remains unchanged even though `(123) 4567` is independently accepted and redacted by `redactContactData`; the slash should end identifier protection before whole-span scoring can absorb that phone.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recognize unspaced periods as identifier boundaries**

When an unscored identifier is immediately followed by a period-separated phone, this predicate rejects every split because it requires whitespace after the period. Thus `ID: 12345678.03.6216.8041` (and its fullwidth equivalent) remains unchanged, although standalone `03.6216.8041` is accepted and redacted; a bare period accepted by `PHONE_SPAN_PATTERN` must permit the independently valid suffix to be classified.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed on exact head `bbfa4fbb501af39bf664bb75601d18314f7e2dcc`. Challenge detection now runs after the bounded body read and before terminal-status selection, independent of `response.ok`. Recognized HTML challenge signatures therefore classify as `challenge_page` for both 2xx and common nonredirect error responses, including the adversarial 503 fixture. The route remains unsuccessful, substantive-content success remains false, the representation digest is retained without body retention, and the closed receipt validator accepts the coherent challenge terminal state.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the link-count check to the opened receipt**

When another process creates a hard-link alias after `lstatSync` returns but before `loadReceiptJson` calls `readFileSync`, this check uses the stale `nlink === 1` value and validation accepts a receipt whose inode is already multiply linked. This affects store/custody validation and both writers, leaving the claimed inode-custody boundary bypassable through a standard check/use race; open the leaf once without following links, inspect and read that descriptor, and recheck its metadata before accepting it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

This P1 concerns boundary ordering when a short identifier and a later parenthesized telephone value occupy one scanner candidate. Final owner-authored commit `547ccb1280ea5b257aeebd509415e74cbfc9274f` closes it through `identifierProtectedPrefixEnd`, `phoneWindowBounds`, `canStartIndependentPhone`, and recursive `phoneRedactionRanges`. The selector now enumerates validated later-phone boundaries before using whole-span scoring as a fallback. A slash, fullwidth slash, period, or guarded whitespace separator can propose a split only when the suffix independently passes telephone validation; scored prefix proposals take precedence, unscored proposals remain subject to the identifier digit floor, and the recursive suffix is classified outside identifier context. The reported `ID: 1234567 / (123) 4567` therefore renders as `ID: 1234567 / [contact omitted]`, with additional regressions for the unspaced slash form, the fullwidth form, and `ID: 1234567.(123)4567`.

The executable map also preserves `ID: 1234567 / 7654321`, `ID: 03.6216.8041`, `ID: 1.212.555.1234`, and the fullwidth North American identifier, so the repair does not turn accepted punctuation into an unconditional split. Commit `547ccb1280ea5b257aeebd509415e74cbfc9274f` and materializer commit `cec0d5d2465b40f4e85dc034dbd674542d6e5f51` share tree `618f0d6b41f96d00188bf6484efc777848fac6e5`, with library blob `ae3d12b009adf77cd9c6a4c070bba7843754b3fc` and test blob `dd71ae0b2e98be8362423b3184ea79215d843978`. Materializer run `32613108541` passed syntax checks, the focused and artifact suites, the complete release gate, pinned-main numstat, exact two-path enforcement, and post-gate custody; artifact `9486090761` records digest `sha256:b8037fb38a4ea26b8a9d517982e030cfa6185d65741178993a3886ac54b17080`. Fresh exact-head Release checks `32613266853`, No magic human gate `32613266863`, and First-party industrial-exhaust intake `32613266868` passed, with the mutating crawl correctly skipped. Can any later parenthesized telephone suffix still be absorbed into identifier protection without first satisfying an independently valid boundary proposal?

This P1 concerns an unscored identifier immediately followed by a period-separated telephone suffix inside one `PHONE_SPAN_PATTERN` candidate. Final owner-authored commit `547ccb1280ea5b257aeebd509415e74cbfc9274f` closes it in `identifierProtectedPrefixEnd`. ASCII and fullwidth periods are now eligible boundary punctuation before whole-span fallback, but a split is accepted only when `canStartIndependentPhone` proves that the suffix is independently telephone-valid. When the complete candidate already scores as one identifier-shaped value, an unscored period proposal also requires at least seven protected prefix digits, which lets `ID: 12345678.03.6216.8041`, `ＩＤ：１２３４５６７８．０３．６２１６．８０４１`, and `ID: 12345678.212.555.1234` redact only the telephone suffix while preserving the identifier and separator.

The wider regression map retains `ID: 12345678.87654321`, `ID: 03.6216.8041`, `ID: 1.212.555.1234`, and `ＩＤ：１．２１２．５５５．１２３４`, so a bare period cannot split an invalid suffix or corrupt a complete period-formatted identifier. Commit `547ccb1280ea5b257aeebd509415e74cbfc9274f` and the qualified materializer commit `cec0d5d2465b40f4e85dc034dbd674542d6e5f51` share tree `618f0d6b41f96d00188bf6484efc777848fac6e5`, library blob `ae3d12b009adf77cd9c6a4c070bba7843754b3fc`, and test blob `dd71ae0b2e98be8362423b3184ea79215d843978`. Materializer run `32613108541` passed the focused suite, artifact suite, complete release gate, pinned-main numstat, exact two-file scope, and post-gate custody; artifact `9486090761` has digest `sha256:b8037fb38a4ea26b8a9d517982e030cfa6185d65741178993a3886ac54b17080`. Fresh exact-head runs `32613266853`, `32613266863`, and `32613266868` passed, with the mutating crawl correctly skipped. Can any period accepted by the scanner still join a protected identifier to an independently valid telephone suffix without either triggering recursive classification or satisfying the complete-identifier guard?

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recurse at the first valid identifier boundary**

When a short identifier is followed by two parenthesized local phones in one scanner span, prioritizing any scored boundary lets the identifier plus the first phone masquerade as a scored prefix. On this exact head, `ID: 1234567 / (123) 4567 / (234) 5678` becomes `ID: 1234567 / (123) 4567 / [contact omitted]`, exposing the first phone; the base redacted both phones. The earlier unscored boundary before `(123) 4567` must remain eligible rather than allowing a later scored proposal that already contains an independently valid telephone.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

This P1 is a boundary-order recursion defect in `identifierProtectedPrefixEnd`, where the scored-prefix selector allowed a later proposal that already contained the first independent telephone value to outrank the earlier valid split. Final owner-authored commit `7f0e6c69cc0d384f9fbfc74fe519bf6e6801c041` closes it by scanning eligible group boundaries from left to right and returning the first admissible boundary. Each slash, fullwidth slash, period, fullwidth period, or whitespace proposal must first leave a suffix that independently satisfies `canStartIndependentPhone`; the existing prefix-score, slash, protected-digit, complete-span, and whitespace guards then decide whether that earliest validated proposal is admissible. Whole-span scoring runs only after no admissible boundary remains. `phoneRedactionRanges` therefore recurses from the boundary before the first phone instead of permitting an identifier-plus-phone prefix to acquire protection.

The executable matrix now requires `ID: 1234567 / (123) 4567 / (234) 5678` to render as `ID: 1234567 / [contact omitted] / [contact omitted]`, with equivalent unspaced-slash, fullwidth, and period-separated forms. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject the x32 syscall namespace**

On x86-64 kernels built with `CONFIG_X86_X32_ABI`, x32 calls use the same audit architecture but set `__X32_SYSCALL_BIT` (`0x40000000`) in the syscall number. These exact comparisons therefore miss calls such as x32 `chmod`, and the filter reaches its allow rule; a helper can place the pathname in low-address memory and bypass every listed metadata denial. Reject the x32 bit or normalize and filter that namespace before accepting the x86-64 architecture proof.

This P2 classifies a self-justifying segmentation predicate in `redactPhoneCandidateAcrossOwnedOuterClosers`. The actors are `closerEvents`, each closer’s sanitized index, `sanitizedCandidate`, `originalIndexes`, preliminary whole-candidate `phoneRedactionRanges`, context-free `boundaryProofRanges`, segment-local context, recursive range translation, and the existing closer-event renderer.

On predecessor `64cf378d5bb7b39b9d496f554a887076cf3d637b`, `initialRanges` were computed under inherited `indeterminatePhoneContext` and then used to decide whether a removed narrative closer was internal to a proved telephone. That allowed overflow-derived authority to manufacture the very cross-boundary interval that suppressed segmentation. Short digit groups could fuse across a real closer, observation bytes could be absorbed, a later intrinsic phone could be joined to an unrelated prefix, and a second intrinsic segment could lose its canonical interval geometry.

The successor retains the ordinary preliminary ranges for rendering, but when incoming context is indeterminate it computes a separate `boundaryProofRanges` set with only overflow-derived authority disabled. Explicit telephone labels and independently complete telephone structure remain available. A closer is suppressed as telephone-internal only when one interval crossing that closer survives the context-free proof. A range that exists only because of inherited bounded context cannot erase the boundary that should terminate that same context. Each closer records its sanitized index when created, later segments begin without inherited overflow authority, and a candidate already handled through segmentation returns terminally rather than falling through into whole-candidate scoring.

For candidates containing many numeric groups after the first redacted phone, this helper is invoked once per seed and rescans every earlier group; each iteration also slices and normalizes the remaining candidate. The period predicate only recognizes a fresh sentence boundary when the period is at the end of the text preceding the current seed, so a later numeric observation can hide an earlier boundary. On exact head, `Phone: 09012345678. 2026-08-17 12:30:45 555-1212` becomes `Phone: [contact omitted]. 2026-08-17 12:30:45 [contact omitted]`: the date seed is correctly refused because it immediately follows the period, but the later time seed sees `. 2026-08-17 ` and reactivates the expired label across the sentence boundary. On exact head, `Phone: 09012345678 12:30:45 555-1212 13:40:50 666-1212` redacts all three phones across three scanner callbacks; the second callback consumes the original lease but renews it, allowing the third callback to inherit again across a second observation. When a labelled phone has an additional value-owned opening wrapper, `contactOffset` leaves that opener in `prefix`, so this check fails to recognize the label and no cross-callback lease is created. On this head, `Phone: ((09012345678)) 12:30:45 555-1212` becomes `Phone: ([contact omitted]) 12:30:45 555-1212`; the same leak occurs for `Phone: (+81 90 1234 5678) ...` and fullwidth forms. Peel accepted opening wrappers before evaluating the label, or otherwise retain the label authority established outside those wrappers.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve nested observations before granting label authority**

When accepted opening wrappers contain a complete numeric observation rather than a phone, peeling them here grants phone-label authority before the observation grammar can claim the value. For example, `Phone: ((2026-08-17)) 12:30:45 555-1212` now becomes `Phone: ([contact omitted]) 12:30:45 [contact omitted]`, corrupting the complete date and minting authority for the later local number; without this peel, the input remains intact. The same regression affects fullwidth dates, long decimals, and unit-bearing observations, so wrapper-aware label matching must not bypass observation custody.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fresh evidence beyond the added non-phone-shaped unit controls is `Phone: ((03-62165111 people)) 12:30:45 555-1212`, which becomes `Phone: ([contact omitted] people)) 12:30:45 555-1212`. Apply wrapper-aware observation matching before scoring the initial interval.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce the declared capture-manifest entry count**

The verifier recomputes a digest over whichever entries remain but never checks `capture_manifest['entry_count']` against the list length or the packet's declared 256-entry denominator. Consequently, removing any unreferenced capture row such as a curl, receipt, result, or stderr record and refreshing the digest fields is accepted even while `entry_count` still says 256, undermining the documented claim that the complete raw-capture manifest is bound.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH during artifact finalization**

When `build:artifact-manifest` is run with a supplied but mismatched `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, passing `env: {}` bypasses the build-clock mismatch check and silently emits a manifest using the admitted timestamp. This contradicts the new clock contract and makes this standalone release command behave differently from the other generators; pass the actual environment so mismatched reproducible-build inputs are rejected.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate all release-manifest identity fields**

If `release-artifact-manifest.json` is altered after finalization, this validator accepts changes to identity metadata such as `version`, `generated`, and `build_clock` because it checks only the schema, source, allowlist, payload inventory, and performance data. For example, changing the version and clock to arbitrary values still makes `validate:artifact` report PASS, so the validation command can greenlight a manifest that misidentifies the release; compare these fields with `package.json` and the admitted build clock as well.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply held directory entries to their descendants**

When a future publication-policy edit adds a file beneath a withheld directory, the equality-only check does not protect it. The policy currently records `build/core-thesis/status-sovereignty` and `reports/core-thesis/status-sovereignty` as exact held paths, but artifact paths are files such as `reports/core-thesis/status-sovereignty/data.json`; adding such a descendant to `paths` would pass both policy validation and the builder's corresponding exact check, publishing material intended to remain blocked. Treat directory-valued holds as prefixes or encode them as prefix rules.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the endpoint key before resolving its URL**

The generated endpoint standalone passes the values from `PATHS` into `loadJson`, but `PATHS` has already replaced the default paths with the configured endpoint values. With the shipped empty defaults this receives `''`, and with a configured API it receives the API URL; neither can be reverse-mapped to `research`, `hops`, etc., so the demo lookup throws `Endpoint release has no demo dataset for ` and configured endpoints are never fetched. The published `Clifford-Number-endpoint.html` therefore fails to initialize in both advertised modes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Redirect legacy hash routes to the explorer**

Replacing the root application's router with `home.js` breaks existing public deep links that still target the root, including `reports/index.html` and both briefing pages (`../#case/...`) plus the README method link. In those flows the browser now loads this homepage, which has no hash router, so “Open case” and previously shared actor/case/method URLs silently land on the causal overview instead of the requested record. Update those links or retain a compatibility redirect for explorer hashes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Render homepage receipt targets as actionable links**

When a user selects any homepage mark or count, the detail panel renders each receipt/source as plain `<li>` text only. The loaded research-source records contain their public URLs, but no anchor or route is emitted here, so users cannot open the exact receipts despite the homepage explicitly promising that every mark and number links directly to them. Render the source URL or an explorer receipt route for each item.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count evidence- and time-filtered actors in the result**

When `evidenceFloor` or `asOf` excludes participants, `filteredOut` is calculated only from the already-filtered `eligible` array. For example, a six-actor roster reduced to two eligible actors returns `totalActors: 6` but only two across `visible + hiddenByBudget + filteredOut`, contradicting this API's accounting guarantee and causing consumers to underreport actors hidden by evidence or temporal filters. Include the ineligible population in the returned accounting, as the existing aperture selector does via `temporalOrEvidenceFiltered`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Add the missing context-base field to Explorer**

Add the corresponding `#public-boundary-research-base` element to `explorer.html`; that template currently contains only `#public-boundary-research`, so this new setter always no-ops. As a result, the Explorer continues to show only the projection timestamp and never exposes the frozen `context_base_as_of` cutoff that distinguishes the mixed source boundary.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count distinct actors before containing a dense surface**

Count unique `actor_id` values rather than actor participation rows here. The ledger explicitly supports multiple legitimate stints for one actor on the same surface, so such a surface can be classified as dense after accumulating more than 19 rows despite having at most 19 actors; the builder would then suppress every participation spoke and publish inflated `actor_count` metadata even though the canonical density policy is defined over distinct actors.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reconcile repeated participant rows before counting edges**

When one participant has multiple stints on a non-dense surface, `addEdge` deduplicates the later rows by `from -> to : topology`, but this increment still counts every row as rendered. The resulting `rendered_participation_edges` exceeds the actual overlay-edge count (breaking the projection invariant), and receipts from later stints are discarded from the surviving edge; merge the participant rows and their receipt IDs or increment only when an edge is actually inserted.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recheck the active view before showing the field**

When the initial Three.js/vendor load is still pending and the user switches to Route, Surface, or a deeper map level, the entry guard has already passed; after the await completes, this unconditionally reactivates WebGL and hides the newly rendered SVG view. Concurrent corpus renders can likewise enter while `renderer` is still null and create multiple renderer instances. Serialize initialization and verify that the current mode is still the corpus map before rendering or activating the field.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pause the renderer when hiding the GPU field**

After a user leaves the corpus map for Route, Surface, or a semantic SVG level, this only hides the host; the 3d-force-graph animation loop and particle rendering continue running against the invisible canvas. Consequently, users spend CPU/GPU and battery for the entire time they inspect other views. Pause the graph when deactivating it and resume it when the WebGL field becomes active again.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
